Let \(S\) be terminal in \(\mathcal G\), suppose no bidirected edge of \(\mathcal G\) is incident to \(S\), and put \(G_V=\mathcal G[V]\).  Fix \(T_0\subseteq V\) and a target cell \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\).  Suppose a finite recursive semi-Markovian SCM \(N\) compatible with \(G_V\) has a finite independent response representation \(\mathcal R^{V}\), a coordinate \(U_0\) with active support \(\mathcal J_0\), strictly positive masses \(u_j\), substantive rows
\[
 c_v(j)=P_{\mathcal R^{V}}(V=v\mid U_0=j),
 \qquad
 h_{x,y}(j)=P_{\mathcal R^{V}}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),U_0=j),
\]
and a vector \(\beta\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J_0}\) such that
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}c_v>0\quad\text{for every }v,\qquad
 \beta^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1=0,\qquad
 \beta^{\mathsf T}c_v=0\quad\text{for every }v,\qquad
 \beta^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}\neq0.
\]
These displayed conditions are the positive ordinary active-coordinate hedge-witness hypothesis.  Let \(\pi_S(1\mid p)\in(0,1)\) be a common terminal selection kernel for every cell \(p\) of \(\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)\), implemented by a finite exogenous response coordinate independent of \(\mathcal R^{V}\), and extend \(N\) by this same kernel.  Define
\[
 q_S(v)=
 \frac{\pi_S(1\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})u^{\mathsf T}c_v}
 {\sum_{v'}\pi_S(1\mid v'_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})u^{\mathsf T}c_{v'}},
 \qquad
 q_0(t)=\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}u^{\mathsf T}c_v.
\]
Then, for every \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\leq\min_v q_S(v)\), this extension gives a compatible input \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\).  Moreover there are \(\eta>0\), a represented baseline \((M,\mathcal R,U_0)\in\mathfrak R_{\epsilon,\eta}^{\circ}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), and the same active direction \(\beta\in\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}^{\perp}\) with \(\beta^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}\neq0\).  Consequently the projective perturbation constructs two finite graph-compatible models \(M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\) that agree exactly on \(q_S,q_0\), have a common positive response-atom lower bound, and satisfy \(\psi_{x,y}(M_1)\neq\psi_{x,y}(M_2)\).

payload.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 G_V=\mathcal G[V].
\]
The premise is failure of ordinary identification on the positive finite substantive model class. Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}kivva\text{-}positive\text{-}ordinary\text{-}id\text{-}specialization}\), applied to \(G_V\) and the cell \((x,y)\), therefore gives finite recursive semi-Markovian substantive SCMs \(N_1,N_2\) compatible with \(G_V\) and a probability table \(p\) such that, for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\),
\[
 P_{N_1}(V=v)=P_{N_2}(V=v)=p(v)>0,
\]
while
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(N_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(N_2).
\]
This is the only step imported from the cited positive ordinary-identification result.

Fix any terminal selection kernel allowed by the statement and abbreviate
\[
 r_v=\pi_S(1\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)}),
 \qquad
 Z=\sum_{v'\in\mathcal X_V}r_{v'}p(v').
\]
Every \(r_v\) and every \(p(v)\) is strictly positive. The state space \(\mathcal X_V\) is finite by \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}state}\), so
\[
 0<Z<\infty.
\]
Because no bidirected edge is incident to \(S\), using an exogenous selection coordinate independent of all substantive exogenous coordinates is compatible with \(\mathcal G\). Because \(S\) is terminal, adjoining its structural equation changes no substantive structural equation and creates no directed feedback. Hence each extension \(M_k\), \(k\in\{1,2\}\), is recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with \(\mathcal G\).

Conditional on \(V=v\), the independent common selection equation has success probability \(r_v\). Thus, for \(k\in\{1,2\}\), the product rule and the common population law give
\[
 P_{M_k}(V=v,S=1)
 =P_{M_k}(S=1\mid V=v)P_{M_k}(V=v)
 =r_vp(v).
\]
Summing this equality over the finite state space yields
\[
 P_{M_k}(S=1)=\sum_v r_vp(v)=Z>0.
\]
Division is therefore licensed, and
\[
 P_{M_k}(V=v\mid S=1)
 =\frac{r_vp(v)}{Z}
 =q_S(v).
\]
The right-hand side does not depend on \(k\). It is a probability table because
\[
 \sum_vq_S(v)=Z^{-1}\sum_vr_vp(v)=1,
\]
and every cell is strictly positive. Likewise marginalization of the common full law gives, for every \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\),
\[
 P_{M_k}(T_0=t)
 =\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}P_{M_k}(V=v)
 =\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}p(v)
 =q_0(t).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_1)
 =\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_2)
 =(q_S,q_0).
\]

Finiteness and strict positivity of the selected table imply
\[
 \min_{v\in\mathcal X_V}q_S(v)>0.
\]
Fix \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\leq\min_vq_S(v)\). The compatibility, positive selection normalizer, and selected-cell inequality established above put each \(M_k\) in \(\mathfrak M_\epsilon(\mathcal G)\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\). Hence the common observed pair lies in \(\mathcal C_\epsilon(\mathcal G,T_0)\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}input\text{-}image}\), and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}observed\text{-}fiber}\) gives
\[
 M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak F_\epsilon(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0).
\]

For an intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\), terminality of \(S\) implies that the selection structural equation is downstream of every substantive variable and is not an input to any substantive equation. The substantive interventional distribution in \(M_k\) is therefore exactly that in \(N_k\). In particular,
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(M_k)=\psi_{x,y}(N_k),\qquad k\in\{1,2\},
\]
so the cited strict inequality yields
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M_2).
\]

It remains to verify, rather than assume, the response-interior assertion. Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\text{-}response\text{-}selection\text{-}admg\text{-}reduction}\) separately to \(M_1\) and \(M_2\). It gives finite independent response representations preserving their full factual laws, the \(T_0\)-margins, and the target intervention cells. In each representation merge response labels inducing the same deterministic maps and delete every zero-mass label. The resulting state space of each coordinate is exactly its positive support. Across the two representations there are only finitely many active coordinate atoms, and every one has strictly positive mass. Therefore
\[
 \eta=\min\{\text{active coordinate-atom masses in either reduced representation}\}>0.
\]
Every active atom in either representation has mass at least \(\eta\), while all equalities already proved are preserved by the reduction. This completes the graph-level positive selection lift.

payload.current: Qiu et al.'s external-data result and the present decision problem overlap only on a restricted boundary. Their Appendix B.2, Condition 2 and Theorem B.5 take \(P(V\mid S=1)\) together with the unbiased covariate margin \(P(T_0)\) and characterize identification of the scalar \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\) under unconfoundedness, treatment overlap, and specified probability classes for the propensity, covariate-outcome law, and selection law. That boundary is contained in the present input signature when \(T_0\) is the covariate block. Their theorem does not decide each scalar cell \(\psi_{x,y}\), or their finite full-table collection \(\boldsymbol\psi\), for an arbitrary finite-state semi-Markovian ADMG, while the present graph-only model does not imply their probability-class restrictions and does not contain their continuous-law examples. Thus the results have a nonempty special-case intersection but neither theorem subsumes the other.
payload.proposed: Qiu et al.'s external-data theorem and the present decision problem are analogues at the level of data slots and estimand mapping; no literal intersection of their model classes is asserted. After relabeling their covariate block as \(T_0\), binary treatment as \(X\), outcome as \(Y\), and observed substantive tuple as \(V\), their selected observational law and external unbiased covariate margin have the same slot pattern \(P(V\mid S=1),P(T_0)\). In any finite specialization with binary \(X\) and numeric \(Y\), \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\) is a finite linear contrast of the cells \(\psi_{x,y}\), so \(\boldsymbol\psi\) determines \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\), whereas the converse fails even for strictly positive finite Markovian DAG models. Qiu et al.'s cited theorem is conditional on unconfoundedness, treatment overlap, and specified probability classes and concludes identification of the scalar \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\), not arbitrary cells \(\psi_{x,y}\) on an arbitrary semi-Markovian \(\mathcal G\). Conversely, the present finite-state graph class neither contains their continuous-law examples nor, from \(\mathcal G\) alone, imposes their probability-class restrictions. Therefore neither theorem subsumes the other.

payload.proof_tex:
Let \(C_Q\), \(D\), and \(R\) denote, respectively, the covariate block, binary treatment, and outcome in \(\mathrm{lem:qiu\text{-}external\text{-}ate\text{-}characterization}\).  Relabel the variables for the purpose of comparing signatures by
\[
T_0=C_Q,\qquad X=\{D\},\qquad Y=\{R\},\qquad
V=C_Q\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{D,R\}.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\), the two entries of the present observation map under (1) are
\[
\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M)
=\bigl(P_M(V\mid S=1),P_M(T_0)\bigr)
=\bigl(P_M(C_Q,D,R\mid S=1),P_M(C_Q)\bigr).
\tag{2}
\]
The cited lemma states that Qiu et al. use a selected observational law together with an external unbiased covariate margin.  Thus (2) proves equality of the two data-slot patterns after relabeling.  It does not assert equality, inclusion, or even nonempty intersection of the two model classes.

We next verify the estimand map.  Suppose only for this calculation that \(R\) has a finite numeric state space and \(D\) is binary.  Every sum below is finite, so no integrability or limiting condition is needed.  The definitions of \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\) and \(\psi_{x,y}\) give, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(M)
&=E_M[R\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1)]
  -E_M[R\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0)]\\
&=\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,
  P_M(R=r\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1))
  -\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,
  P_M(R=r\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0))\\
&=\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,\psi_{1,r}(M)
  -\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,\psi_{0,r}(M).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
Hence the finite table \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)\), whose coordinatewise role is made explicit in \(\mathrm{def:full\text{-}kernel\text{-}collection}\), determines \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(M)\) through the displayed linear map.

The converse to this last implication fails inside a strictly positive finite Markovian DAG subclass.  Consider the graph \(D\to R\) with \(S\) isolated, take \(X=\{D\}\), \(Y=\{R\}\), and let \(T_0=\varnothing\).  Let \(U_D\) and \(U_S\) be independent Bernoulli\((1/2)\) variables, and let \(U_R\) be independent of them and uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,12\}\).  In model \(M_j\), set
\[
D=U_D,\qquad S=U_S,
\qquad
R_1=\mathbf 1\{U_R\le 3+6D\},
\qquad
R_2=\mathbf 1\{U_R\le 4+6D\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Each model is finite and recursive.  Its exogenous variables are mutually independent, so it is Markovian and therefore semi-Markovian; its structural equations follow the displayed DAG.  Also \(P_{M_j}(S=1)=1/2>0\).  Independence of \(S\) from \((D,R_j)\) yields the selected cell tables
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
&(D,R_j)=(0,1)&(0,0)&(1,1)&(1,0)\\ \hline
j=1&1/8&3/8&3/8&1/8\\
j=2&1/6&1/3&5/12&1/12.
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Every cell in (5) is positive; in fact both models satisfy the selected-cell lower bound \(1/12\).  Thus the positivity assertion uses no boundary point.  Intervention replaces the equation \(D=U_D\) and leaves the equation for \(R_j\) unchanged, so (4) gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc|c}
&P_{M_j}(R=1\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0))
&P_{M_j}(R=1\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1))
&\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(M_j)\\ \hline
j=1&3/12&9/12&6/12\\
j=2&4/12&10/12&6/12.
\end{array}
\tag{6}
\]
Both scalar effects equal \(1/2\), while \(\psi_{0,1}(M_1)=1/4\ne1/3=\psi_{0,1}(M_2)\).  Therefore the linear map in (3) is not injective even on the stated positive finite DAG subclass: identification of the scalar effect alone cannot decide every coordinate of \(\boldsymbol\psi\).

It remains to establish the two scope separations.  By \(\mathrm{lem:qiu\text{-}external\text{-}ate\text{-}characterization}\), Qiu et al.'s theorem assumes unconfoundedness, treatment overlap on the covariate support, and a pairwise distinguishability condition on specified classes of propensity, covariate--potential-outcome, and selection laws.  Its conclusion identifies the single scalar \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\), not every cell \(\psi_{x,y}\) for arbitrary semi-Markovian \(\mathcal G\).  Equation (6) additionally shows why the scalar conclusion cannot be inverted into the full-table conclusion.  Thus the cited theorem does not subsume the present arbitrary-cell graph problem.

Conversely, \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) restricts the present class to finite-state recursive semi-Markovian models and imposes only the listed graph, selection, and selected-cell positivity conditions.  The cited lemma states both that Qiu et al.'s exposition includes continuous covariate--outcome laws with densities and that its identification criterion is indexed by separately specified probability classes.  Continuous-law examples are not members of the present finite-state class.  Moreover, a graph \(\mathcal G\) and the membership conditions in \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) do not supply a chosen triple of probability classes or assert Qiu et al.'s pairwise distinguishability condition.  Hence the present graph class does not subsume the cited setup.  Together with (2), (3), and (6), these observations prove precisely an input-shape and estimand-map analogy, the failure of the reverse estimand map, and non-subsumption in both directions, without claiming a literal model-class intersection.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\epsilon>0\), an input \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), a model \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), and a cell \((x,y)\). By Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}observed\text{-}fiber}\),
\[
 q_S(v)=P_M(V=v\mid S=1),
 \qquad
 q_0(t)=P_M(T_0=t).
\]
Moreover, Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}input\text{-}image}\) give \(P_M(S=1)>0\) and \(q_S(v)\geq\epsilon>0\) for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\). Hence
\[
 P_M(V=v)\geq P_M(V=v,S=1)
 =P_M(S=1)q_S(v)
 \geq P_M(S=1)\epsilon>0.
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus the full population law is strictly positive at every substantive cell, and every one of its marginal conditioning cells is positive.

Suppose first that \(T_0=V\). The population-initialization clause of Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) puts, for each \(v\in\mathcal X_V\), the key
\[
 (V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},v,\ast,\ast)
\]
in the initial state with annotation
\[
 q_0(v)=P_M(T_0=v)=P_M(V=v).
 \tag{2}
\]
Consider any finite, cellwise derivation of \(P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\) from \(P_M(V)\) using ordinary finite probability manipulations and the three rules of do-calculus. We prove inductively over that derivation that the scalar key produced at each step becomes present in the saturation state. Every initial scalar is present by (2). For the induction step, all finitely many input keys are present. If the step is a probability manipulation, its marginalization, conditioning, or chain instance is one of the complete scalar moves in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\). A division is used only at a positive conditioning cell. Positivity for conditionals formed directly from the observational law follows from (1), and positivity of any other conditioning cell used is part of the legality of the stipulated cellwise derivation. If the step is do-calculus, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}rules}\) and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}graphical\text{-}fixing\text{-}moves}\) give the corresponding population-tagged move and equality of its input and output kernels.

In either case, the move instance lies in the finite universe \(\mathscr U\), its complete input-key set is present, and its graphical and denominator premises hold. If its output is absent, it remains enabled because Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) only adds keys. It cannot be postponed forever: each earlier selected move adds a previously absent key, while Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}extid\text{-}sound\text{-}termination}\) bounds the number of present keys by \(\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert\). A terminal state omitting that output would therefore contradict the rule that failure occurs only when no enabled instance has an absent output. This completes the induction.

The target key \((Y,X,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},y,x,\ast)\) consequently becomes present and is checked before the next transition. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}extid\text{-}storage\text{-}invariant}\) identifies its annotation, throughout the exact fiber, with
\[
 k^M_{(Y,X,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop})}(y\mid x,\ast)
 =P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
 =\psi_{x,y}(M).
 \tag{3}
\]
The returned expression belongs to \(\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\) by Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}arithmetic\text{-}language}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\). Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}ordinary\text{-}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}completeness}\) supplies such a finite ordinary derivation whenever the cell is identifiable from the full observational law, proving the first reduction.

Suppose next that \(\mathcal G\) entails \(S\perp\!\!\!\perp V\). Selected initialization provides
\[
 (V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{sel},v,\ast,\ast)
 \quad\text{with annotation}\quad q_S(v)
\]
for every \(v\). With \(A=V\) and \(B=C=\varnothing\), the population-storage predicate in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}source\text{-}bridge\text{-}moves}\) is exactly \(V\perp\!\!\!\perp S\). Saturation therefore makes the corresponding population key present, unless it is already present, and preserves its annotation. The storage invariant then gives
\[
 q_S(v)=P_M(V=v\mid S=1)=P_M(V=v),
 \tag{4}
\]
where conditioning is defined because \(P_M(S=1)>0\). Thus the same full-population scalar keys are available with the claimed annotations.

Now let \(T_0=\varnothing\). Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) says that the unique trivial margin contributes no scalar key. A margin-extension instance requires a nonempty population-margin input key, so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}source\text{-}bridge\text{-}moves}\) makes no such instance admissible. Initially every present key is selected-tagged. Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}graphical\text{-}fixing\text{-}moves}\) preserve source tags. The only source-changing moves are margin extension and population storage; the former is unavailable, while the latter maps
\[
 (A,B,C,\mathrm{sel},a,b,c)
 \longmapsto
 (A,B,C,\mathrm{pop},a,b,c)
 \tag{5}
\]
with unchanged annotation exactly when
\[
 A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C
 \quad\text{in }G_{\overline B}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Induction on the number of transitions shows that every selected key belongs to the closure of selected initialization under selected probability and graphical-fixing moves, and that every population key is either an output (5) satisfying (6) or follows from such outputs by population probability and graphical-fixing moves. Conversely, any absent output in these closures whose complete inputs are present remains enabled. Finiteness and the preceding no-permanent-postponement argument show that saturation adds it before termination. Hence the resulting closure has exactly the asserted keys. Setting \(B=C=\varnothing\) in (6) gives unconditional selection independence.

Finally, suppose margin extension reconstructs every cell of the full population law. Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}margin\text{-}extension}\) gives, at each reconstructed cell \((t,z)\),
\[
 P_M(T_0=t,Z=z)
 =P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t,S=1)q_0(t),
 \tag{7}
\]
and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}extid\text{-}storage\text{-}invariant}\) says that the transition annotation is the right-hand side of (7). Taking \(Z=V\setminus T_0\), or composing reconstructed population blocks by the probability moves, makes every key
\[
 (V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},v,\ast,\ast)
\]
present with annotation \(P_M(V=v)\). The replay argument leading to (3) now applies. In particular, under an adjustment criterion with adjustment block \(L\), it returns
\[
 P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
 =\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal X_L}
 P_M(Y=y\mid X=x,L=\ell)P_M(L=\ell),
 \tag{8}
\]
and under the corresponding front-door criterion with mediating block \(D\), it returns
\[
 P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
 =\sum_{d\in\mathcal X_D}P_M(D=d\mid X=x)
 \sum_{x'\in\mathcal X_X}
 P_M(Y=y\mid D=d,X=x')P_M(X=x').
 \tag{9}
\]
The named graphical criteria are precisely the premises making the usual do-calculus derivations of (8)--(9) legal; Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}rules}\) validates each graphical equality, and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\) realizes the finite sums, products, and positive divisions.

Apply (3) to every successful \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\). Each returned coordinate equals its coordinate of \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)\) throughout the exact fiber. If all runs succeed, Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}kernel\text{-}collection}\) forms \(\mathbf F\) in the same order, so
\[
 \mathbf F(q_S,q_0)
 =\bigl(F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0):(x,y)\in\mathcal I\bigr)^{\mathsf T}
 =\bigl(\psi_{x,y}(M):(x,y)\in\mathcal I\bigr)^{\mathsf T}
 =\boldsymbol\psi(M).
\]
If some run fails, \(\mathbf F\) is not formed, while the proved coordinatewise equality remains valid for every returned cell. This proves all four reductions and the collection claim.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathcal G\) be an arbitrary finite selection ADMG on \(V\cup\{S\}\), and put \(G_V=\mathcal G[V]\). Fix \(T_0\subseteq V\) and \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\). Suppose \(\psi_{x,y}\) is not identifiable from the full observational law \(P(V)\) over the positive finite recursive semi-Markovian substantive SCMs compatible with \(G_V\). Then there exist two such substantive models \(N_1,N_2\) and a strictly positive common table \(p\) such that
\[
 P_{N_1}(V=v)=P_{N_2}(V=v)=p(v)>0
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(N_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(N_2).
\]
For any common strictly positive table \(\pi_S(1\mid r)\in(0,1)\), indexed by cells \(r\) of \(\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)\), there are edge-silent extensions \(M_1,M_2\) compatible with the full graph \(\mathcal G\): the equation for \(S\) realizes \(\pi_S\) using an independent finite response coordinate and ignores every exogenous coordinate displayed by a bidirected edge incident to \(S\); every substantive equation retains its equation from \(N_k\), ignores a displayed parent \(S\), and ignores every exogenous coordinate displayed by a bidirected edge incident to \(S\). Define
\[
 q_S(v)=
 \frac{\pi_S(1\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v)}
 {\sum_{v'}\pi_S(1\mid v'_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v')},
 \qquad
 q_0(t)=\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}p(v).
\]
For every \(\epsilon\) satisfying \(0<\epsilon\leq\min_v q_S(v)\),
\[
 (q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0),
 \qquad
 M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0),
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_1)=\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_2)=(q_S,q_0),
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M_2).
\]
The two extensions admit finite independent response representations such that, after zero-mass response labels are deleted, every active atom in either representation has mass at least one common witness-specific constant \(\eta>0\). Consequently ordinary positive-model nonidentifiability implies two-law nonidentifiability over the full positive \(\mathcal G\)-compatible model class for every \(T_0\), because the edge-silent extensions form a subclass of that class.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(G_V=\mathcal G[V]\). Semantic nonidentifiability means that the query is not constant on at least one fiber of the full observational-law map. The positive finite separating pair is supplied by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}kivva\text{-}positive\text{-}ordinary\text{-}id\text{-}specialization}\), which gives substantive models \(N_1,N_2\) compatible with \(G_V\) and a table \(p\) satisfying
\[
 P_{N_1}(V=v)=P_{N_2}(V=v)=p(v)>0
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
 \tag{1}
\]
and
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(N_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(N_2).
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus the cited positive ordinary-identification result is used only for (1)--(2). By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\text{-}response\text{-}selection\text{-}admg\text{-}reduction}\), we may choose finite independent response representations of \(N_1,N_2\) preserving their complete factual and counterfactual laws. Delete zero-mass response labels; hence every remaining coordinate atom has positive mass.

We next construct the extensions rather than assuming their existence. Let
\[
 \mathcal H_S
 =\bigl\{g:\mathcal X_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}\bigr\}.
\]
This is finite by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}state}\). Introduce an exogenous coordinate \(U_S\), independent of all substantive coordinates, with
\[
 P(U_S=g)
 =\prod_{r\in\mathcal X_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)}}
 \pi_S(1\mid r)^{g(r)}
 \{1-\pi_S(1\mid r)\}^{1-g(r)}.
 \tag{3}
\]
The empty-parent case uses the unique empty-block cell. Repeated finite distributivity gives
\[
 \sum_{g\in\mathcal H_S}P(U_S=g)
 =\prod_r\{\pi_S(1\mid r)+1-\pi_S(1\mid r)\}=1.
\]
Every factor in (3) is strictly positive, so every atom of \(U_S\) has positive mass. Define
\[
 S=U_S\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)\bigr).
 \tag{4}
\]
For every bidirected edge incident to \(S\), take its displayed shared exogenous coordinate to have one atom of mass one and make both incident structural equations ignore that coordinate. For every \(W\in V\), retain the substantive equation from \(N_k\); if \(S\) is a displayed parent of \(W\), extend the equation constantly in its \(S\)-argument. Thus every substantive equation also ignores the coordinates displayed by bidirected edges incident to \(S\).

We verify compatibility explicitly. Under the nonparametric ADMG convention in Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}semi\text{-}markovian}\), a structural function may depend only on displayed directed parents and its allowed exogenous coordinates; it is not required to depend nontrivially on every displayed argument. Indeed, if \(f(d,u)\) is an allowed function of a subset of displayed arguments, then \(\widetilde f(d,e,u)=f(d,u)\) is a function on the full displayed argument space, constant in the unused coordinate \(e\). Such constant extension introduces no unauthorized directed or bidirected dependence. The equations just constructed therefore use only arguments permitted by \(\mathcal G\). Their exogenous coordinates are independent, and each shared coordinate is incident to at most its displayed pair. Finally, the directed part of \(\mathcal G\) is acyclic, so evaluating these equations in a topological order is recursive even when \(S\) is not terminal. Hence each \(M_k\) is recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with the full arbitrary graph \(\mathcal G\).

Because every substantive equation ignores \(S\), \(U_S\), and every \(S\)-incident shared coordinate, the factual vector \(V\) is exactly the factual vector generated by \(N_k\). The same observation holds after any intervention on a subset of \(V\). Therefore (1)--(2) imply
\[
 P_{M_k}(V=v)=p(v),
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(M_k)=\psi_{x,y}(N_k),
 \quad k\in\{1,2\},
 \tag{5}
\]
and in particular
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M_2).
 \tag{6}
\]
This is the step that removes the former terminality and selection-unconfoundedness restrictions.

Equation (3) also makes \(U_S\) independent of \(V\). For a fixed parent cell \(r\), summing (3) over all response maps with \(g(r)=1\) gives
\[
 P\{U_S(r)=1\}
 =\pi_S(1\mid r)
 \prod_{r'\ne r}\{\pi_S(1\mid r')+1-\pi_S(1\mid r')\}
 =\pi_S(1\mid r).
 \tag{7}
\]
Consequently, for every substantive cell \(v\), (4), (5), and (7) give
\[
 P_{M_k}(V=v,S=1)
 =\pi_S(1\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v).
 \tag{8}
\]
Let
\[
 Z_S=\sum_{v'}\pi_S(1\mid v'_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v').
\]
All summands are strictly positive, and there are finitely many cells, so \(0<Z_S<\infty\). Summing (8) yields \(P_{M_k}(S=1)=Z_S\). Division is therefore licensed, and
\[
 P_{M_k}(V=v\mid S=1)
 =\frac{\pi_S(1\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v)}{Z_S}
 =q_S(v).
 \tag{9}
\]
The right-hand side is common to the two models, sums to one, and is strictly positive at every cell. Marginalizing (5) gives, for every \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\),
\[
 P_{M_k}(T_0=t)
 =\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}p(v)
 =q_0(t).
 \tag{10}
\]
Equations (9)--(10) and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\) show
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_1)
 =\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_2)
 =(q_S,q_0).
 \tag{11}
\]

Finiteness and cellwise strict positivity imply \(\min_vq_S(v)>0\). Fix \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\leq\min_vq_S(v)\). The compatibility proved above, \(P_{M_k}(S=1)=Z_S>0\), and (9) put \(M_k\) in \(\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G)\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\). Equation (11) and Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}input\text{-}image}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}observed\text{-}fiber}\) then give
\[
 (q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0),
 \qquad
 M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0).
 \tag{12}
\]

It remains to check the response-interior conclusion. The reduced representations of \(N_1,N_2\) have finitely many active coordinate atoms of positive mass. The selection coordinate in (3) has finitely many positive atoms, and every ignored \(S\)-incident coordinate has its single atom of mass one. Hence the union of the active coordinate-atom masses across both extensions is a finite nonempty set of positive real numbers. Its minimum
\[
 \eta
 =\min\{\text{active coordinate-atom masses in either extension}\}
 >0
 \tag{13}
\]
is a common witness-specific slack. Equations (6), (11), and (12) exhibit two members of one exact two-law fiber with different query values. Because these edge-silent models are members of, hence a subclass of, the full positive \(\mathcal G\)-compatible class, a functional valid on that superclass would have to take one value on their common input, contradicting (6). This monotonic superclass argument proves two-law nonidentifiability. It does not assert the invalid reverse implication that identification on the edge-silent subclass would establish identification on the full superclass.
added_lemmas.justification: This all-graph edge-silent lift proves that ordinary positive-model nonidentifiability survives the selected conditional and every external margin inside the full graph-compatible superclass.
added_lemmas.gap: The ordinary positive witness supplies a common full law; the new construction activates no displayed edge at selection, proves full-graph compatibility, preserves the normalized selected law and every margin exactly, and retains query separation.
added_lemmas.consumer: It is the graph-level necessary obstruction for every external-margin recovery claim and the necessary half of the terminal full-margin equivalence.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathcal G\) be any finite selection ADMG on \(V\cup\{S\}\), put \(G_V=\mathcal G[V]\), fix \(T_0\subseteq V\), and fix \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\). If \(\psi_{x,y}\) is identifiable from \((P_M(V\mid S=1),P_M(T_0))\) over the full class of positive finite recursive semi-Markovian models compatible with \(\mathcal G\), then \(\psi_{x,y}\) is identifiable from \(P_N(V)\) over the positive finite substantive model class compatible with \(G_V\). If \(S\) is terminal and \(T_0=V\), the converse also holds, without any restriction on bidirected edges incident to \(S\); hence on that boundary the two identification statements are equivalent. Moreover, for every \(\epsilon>0\), every compatible input \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,V)\), and every ordinarily identifiable cell, \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) returns a finite arithmetic expression \(F_{x,y}\in\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\) satisfying
\[
 F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M)
\]
for every \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,V;q_S,q_0)\). No converse from a bare \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We prove the necessary direction by contraposition. Suppose \(\psi_{x,y}\) is not identifiable from \(P_N(V)\) over the positive finite substantive model class compatible with \(G_V\). Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}all\text{-}graph\text{-}positive\text{-}ordinary\text{-}selection\text{-}lift}\) supplies edge-silent models \(M_1,M_2\) compatible with the full arbitrary graph \(\mathcal G\) such that
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_1)=\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_2)
 \quad\text{but}\quad
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M_2).
 \tag{1}
\]
Their selected tables are strictly positive, so both belong to the full positive graph-compatible model class. If a single two-law identifying map existed on that full class, applying it to the common left-hand input in (1) would force the two right-hand query values to be equal. This contradiction proves the contrapositive. The reasoning uses a separating subclass to refute identification on its superclass; it makes no reverse claim from subclass identification.

Now suppose \(S\) is terminal and \(T_0=V\). The necessary implication just proved does not require terminality. For the converse, assume ordinary identification on \(G_V\), and let \(f\) be its identifying map, so
\[
 f(P_N(V))=\psi_{x,y}(N)
 \tag{2}
\]
for every positive finite substantive model \(N\) compatible with \(G_V\). Take any positive finite model \(M\) compatible with \(\mathcal G\). Delete the equation for \(S\) and retain all substantive equations and exogenous coordinates. Terminality means that \(S\) is not a directed parent of any substantive vertex, so no retained equation uses \(S\). A coordinate represented by a bidirected edge \(S\leftrightarrow W\) can remain as a private disturbance of \(W\) after \(S\) is deleted; it is independent of the other exogenous coordinates and affects at most that one retained equation. Thus the retained system, denoted \(N_M\), is recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with \(G_V\), even when bidirected edges are incident to \(S\). Deletion changes neither the factual law on \(V\) nor any intervention on \(V\), whence
\[
 P_{N_M}(V)=P_M(V),
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(N_M)=\psi_{x,y}(M).
 \tag{3}
\]

The ordinary positivity premise required in (2) follows from selected positivity rather than being added silently. If \(P_M(S=1)>0\) and \(P_M(V=v\mid S=1)>0\), then
\[
 P_M(V=v)
 \geq P_M(V=v,S=1)
 =P_M(S=1)P_M(V=v\mid S=1)>0
 \tag{4}
\]
for every \(v\). Because \(T_0=V\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\) gives \(q_0=P_M(V)\). Combining (2)--(4), the explicit two-law map
\[
 F(q_S,q_0)=f(q_0)
 \tag{5}
\]
satisfies \(F(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M)\) for every positive model compatible with \(\mathcal G\). This proves the converse and the exact terminal full-margin equivalence without excluding incident bidirected edges.

For the executable claim, fix \(\epsilon>0\) and \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,V)\). Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}ordinary\text{-}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}completeness}\) provides a finite ordinary do-calculus and probability derivation of every ordinarily identifiable cell from \(q_0=P(V)\) on \(G_V\). Its graphical separation predicates remain valid in \(\mathcal G\): every path between substantive vertices that is absent from \(G_V\) but present in \(\mathcal G\) must pass through \(S\); because \(S\) is terminal, both incident edges have arrowheads at \(S\), and \(S\) has no directed descendant. Thus \(S\) is an unconditioned collider with no conditioned descendant in every relevant mutilated graph, since the conditioning blocks are subsets of \(V\). Such a path is blocked. Hence the ordinary derivation is a legal population-tagged derivation in the transition system.

Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}boundary\text{-}reductions}\) now applies: full-margin initialization stores every cell of \(q_0=P(V)\), and saturation replays that finite derivation. It returns some \(F_{x,y}\in\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\). Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}extid\text{-}sound\text{-}termination}\) then yields, for every \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,V;q_S,q_0)\),
\[
 F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M).
 \tag{6}
\]
This argument proves success only on the terminal full-margin boundary for ordinarily identifiable cells and does not turn \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) into a general nonidentification certificate.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the all-graph necessity result, together with the exact ordinary-ID equivalence when the external margin is the full population law and selection is terminal.
added_lemmas.gap: The all-graph direction requires a same-input separating subclass; the converse requires proving that terminal deletion preserves the substantive factual and interventional model even with bidirected edges incident to selection.
added_lemmas.consumer: It gives the first decisive gate for the ACTG generalization and an executable iff audit on the terminal full-margin boundary.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The terminal and selection-unconfounded theorem is obsolete because the edge-silent construction proves the strictly stronger result for every selection ADMG; migrating inbound edges avoids retaining a redundant weaker numbered theorem.
The necessary direction now holds for every selection ADMG and the terminal full-margin equivalence no longer needs selection-unconfoundedness, so the former narrower proposition is obsolete.

proposed.comparator_claim: The cited work treats the nonparametric selected-conditional-plus-external-margin problem under common positive laws and proves IDSB sound while leaving completeness unresolved; the present finite epsilon-positive class is a specialization, not the same class.
Do-search is sound and terminating for its input language, but its negative-answer guarantee does not cover unrestricted generalized-identifiability Row 8 inputs of the present two-source shape.

The published continuous probability-class theorem studies scalar ATE identification from a selected observational law and an unbiased covariate margin; it is an input-shape and estimand analogue, not a literal finite-discrete model-class intersection.

Ordinary ID and do-calculus are complete from the full observational law without a global positivity guarantee; on the terminal full-margin boundary the present two-law positive-model problem is equivalent to ordinary positive-model identification, but the positive separating pair is not attributed to this source.

Definition 5 and Theorems 1--2 provide the positive graph/algorithmic completeness bridge and finite construction for an ordinary same-P(V) separating pair; the present theorem lifts that pair edge-silently to every selection ADMG and every external margin.
SS-ID is sound for a different context-selected data-fusion likelihood and completeness is conjectured there.
One-law ADMG identification functionals can be compiled into influence-function estimators in the classes treated there.

The ACTG 320 target effect is estimated from trial data and individual-level target-population covariates under transport assumptions; the WIHS or CNICS external-margin use here is an audit consumer, not evidence for the theorem.
Finite discrete causal queries under arbitrary evidence admit response-function polynomial formulations useful for the unexecuted exact-fiber audit.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The comparator map must name the all-graph replacement results and distinguish the precise positive, generalized-identifiability, and continuous probability-class scopes required by the directive.

prose_updates.tldr: The note gives a terminating, sound cellwise procedure for recovering \(\psi_{x,y}(M)=P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\) from \(q_S=P(V\mid S=1)\) and one unbiased margin \(q_0=P(T_0)\), and it now proves an all-graph necessary obstruction. For every finite selection ADMG, ordinary positive-model nonidentifiability on the substantive graph survives both observed laws: an edge-silent pair of full-graph-compatible models shares the normalized selected table and every \(T_0\)-margin but disagrees on the query. When \(S\) is terminal and \(T_0=V\), two-law identification is exactly equivalent to ordinary positive-model identification, with no exclusion of bidirected edges incident to \(S\), and EXT-ID replays every ordinarily identifiable cell. This is a necessary transfer and a boundary equivalence, not universal two-law completeness: a bare EXT-ID failure still has no general exact-fiber implication, the margin-anchored hedge remains open, and the proposed three-node quantifier-elimination audit has not been executed. Finite-table inference remains supporting material.

project_justification.gap: Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim formulate the nonparametric selected-conditional-plus-external-margin problem under common positive laws and prove IDSB sound while leaving completeness unresolved; the present finite epsilon-positive class is a specialization rather than the identical class. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen encode the two sources in generalized-identifiability Row 8, for which their negative-answer completeness result does not apply. Qiu et al. prove a scalar-ATE probability-class characterization in their literal published continuous setup, not arbitrary finite-state semi-Markovian ADMG recovery. The missing universal result is still a same-input witness for every failed mixed-source recursion.
project_justification.niche: The closed contribution is a graph-native necessary obstruction valid for every selection ADMG, obtained by embedding an ordinary positive separating pair as an edge-silent compatible subclass, plus an exact terminal full-margin equivalence. This isolates what no external margin can repair before attempting the harder margin-anchored failure-completeness theorem.
project_justification.fill: The note defines the exact two-law image and fiber, a bounded source-tagged saturation machine, and sound arithmetic outputs. It proves that displayed arrows or bidirected edges at selection need not be active for compatibility, constructs finite edge-silent extensions with a common response-atom slack, derives their identical normalized selected law and arbitrary external margin, and uses monotonic superclass logic to obtain all-graph necessity. Terminal deletion then yields the full-margin converse and EXT-ID replay. The named three-node witness, symbolic real-closed-field audit, and universal margin-anchored hedge remain ordered open gates; no universal completeness claim is made.

prose_updates.related_work: Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim (2019, Definition 4, Algorithms 2--3, Theorem 4, and printed pages 2749--2750) study the nonparametric selected-conditional-plus-external-margin problem with common positive laws and prove IDSB sound while leaving completeness unresolved; the note's finite epsilon-positive model class is a specialization, not an identification of classes. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2021, Section 2.1, Table 1, Algorithm 2, and Theorems 2--3) can encode both input laws and prove soundness and termination, but their negative-answer guarantee covers Rows 1--4 and 6, not generalized-identifiability Row 8, where the present pair resides. Qiu et al. (2026, arXiv:2605.13430v3, Definition 2.2, Condition 1, Theorem 3.1, Appendix B.2 Condition 2, and Theorem B.5) characterize scalar ATE identification over specified propensity, covariate--outcome, and selection-law classes in the literal published continuous setup. Their data slots and estimand map are analogous to the present special boundary, but neither model class subsumes the other. Semantic nonidentifiability over positive finite models already asks for a same-observational-law separating pair; Kivva et al. (2022, Definition 5 and Theorems 1--2) provide the positive graph/algorithmic completeness bridge and finite construction used here. Shpitser and Pearl (2006, Theorems 4--6) supply the ordinary ID and do-calculus obstruction without global positivity and are not the source of the positive witness. The new step is the all-graph edge-silent extension preserving a normalized selected conditional and every external margin. Richardson et al. (2023) inform the successful fixing branches; Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser (2024) analyze a different systematic-selection likelihood; Duarte et al. (2024) provide response-function polynomial machinery for the still-unexecuted exact-fiber audit. Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (2022) inform graphical influence-function compilation. Li, Buchanan, and Cole (2022) provide the ACTG 320 benchmark with richer individual-level target covariates; WIHS or CNICS margins are an applied audit consumer rather than theorem evidence.
prose_updates.interpretation: The all-graph obstruction is a one-way diagnostic. If the substantive ADMG does not identify the target from a positive full population law, then no method can identify it uniformly over the unrestricted two-law graph-compatible class merely by adding a selected conditional and any one margin \(P(T_0)\): the edge-silent witness pair already defeats such a method. Identification on that edge-silent subclass would not establish identification on the full superclass. When selection is terminal and the external margin is the entire \(P(V)\), deletion of selection preserves the substantive model even with incident bidirected edges, so the diagnostic becomes an equivalence and EXT-ID is executable. For the ACTG 320 generalization, this separates a necessary graph audit from any additional transport, probability-class, or data-rich assumptions justified for WIHS or CNICS.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The edge-silent theorem proves only a necessary transfer from ordinary positive-model nonidentifiability and does not characterize all information contributed by a selected law and a proper external margin. It uses a compatible subclass in which displayed selection-adjacent arguments are inactive; the reverse direction from identification on this subclass to the full compatible superclass is invalid and is not claimed. EXT-ID soundness and termination do not imply that \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) yields a separating exact-fiber pair. Universal two-law completeness, the margin-anchored hedge, and the parameterized three-node real-closed-field elimination remain unresolved, and no QE3 execution is reported. Presolve values such as \(19/36\) and the positive \(A\to Y\to S\) pair with intervention values \(1/3\) and \(2/3\) remain diagnostics only. The inference results apply only to differentiable returned functionals on fixed positive compact subclasses.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Termination holds for every syntactically valid cell input; soundness and boundary claims hold on the compatible image \(\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\) and its exact fibers. The all-graph theorem gives a witness-specific \(\epsilon>0\) and response-atom slack \(\eta>0\); it proves that ordinary positive-model failure implies failure over the full two-law graph-compatible superclass for every \(T_0\). It does not prove the converse for a proper margin, does not certify any bare EXT-ID failure, and does not establish universal two-law completeness. Exact equivalence and guaranteed EXT-ID replay are claimed only when \(S\) is terminal and \(T_0=V\), although bidirected edges may be incident to \(S\). At \(T_0=\varnothing\), margin extension disappears but graphically licensed population storage remains. Do-search has no failure-completeness theorem for unrestricted Row 8, and Qiu et al.'s result remains a disjoint-support input-shape and scalar-estimand analogue under its published continuous probability-class setup. No QE3 execution or exhaustive observed-table enumeration is claimed. The ACTG 320 use with WIHS or CNICS margins is a downstream audit consumer, not evidence for any theorem.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\epsilon>0\), an input \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), a model \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), and a cell \((x,y)\). By Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}observed\text{-}fiber}\),
\[
 q_S(v)=P_M(V=v\mid S=1),
 \qquad
 q_0(t)=P_M(T_0=t).
\]
Moreover, Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}input\text{-}image}\) give \(P_M(S=1)>0\) and \(q_S(v)\geq\epsilon>0\) for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\). Hence
\[
 P_M(V=v)\geq P_M(V=v,S=1)
 =P_M(S=1)q_S(v)
 \geq P_M(S=1)\epsilon>0.
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus the full population law is strictly positive at every substantive cell, and every one of its marginal conditioning cells is positive.

Suppose first that \(T_0=V\). The population-initialization clause of Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) puts, for each \(v\in\mathcal X_V\), the key
\[
 (V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},v,\ast,\ast)
\]
in the initial state with annotation
\[
 q_0(v)=P_M(T_0=v)=P_M(V=v).
 \tag{2}
\]
Consider any finite, cellwise derivation of \(P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\) from \(P_M(V)\) using ordinary finite probability manipulations and the three rules of do-calculus. We prove inductively over that derivation that the scalar key produced at each step becomes present in the saturation state. Every initial scalar is present by (2). For the induction step, all finitely many input keys are present. If the step is a probability manipulation, its marginalization, conditioning, or chain instance is one of the complete scalar moves in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\). A division is used only at a positive conditioning cell. Positivity for conditionals formed directly from the observational law follows from (1), and positivity of any other conditioning cell used is part of the legality of the stipulated cellwise derivation. If the step is do-calculus, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}rules}\) and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}graphical\text{-}fixing\text{-}moves}\) give the corresponding population-tagged move and equality of its input and output kernels.

In either case, the move instance lies in the finite universe \(\mathscr U\), its complete input-key set is present, and its graphical and denominator premises hold. If its output is absent, it remains enabled because Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) only adds keys. It cannot be postponed forever: each earlier selected move adds a previously absent key, while Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}extid\text{-}sound\text{-}termination}\) bounds the number of present keys by \(\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert\). A terminal state omitting that output would therefore contradict the rule that failure occurs only when no enabled instance has an absent output. This completes the induction.

The target key \((Y,X,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},y,x,\ast)\) consequently becomes present and is checked before the next transition. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}extid\text{-}storage\text{-}invariant}\) identifies its annotation, throughout the exact fiber, with
\[
 k^M_{(Y,X,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop})}(y\mid x,\ast)
 =P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
 =\psi_{x,y}(M).
 \tag{3}
\]
The returned expression belongs to \(\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\) by Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}arithmetic\text{-}language}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\). Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}ordinary\text{-}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}completeness}\) supplies such a finite ordinary derivation whenever the cell is identifiable from the full observational law, proving the first reduction.

Suppose next that \(\mathcal G\) entails \(S\perp\!\!\!\perp V\). Selected initialization provides
\[
 (V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{sel},v,\ast,\ast)
 \quad\text{with annotation}\quad q_S(v)
\]
for every \(v\). With \(A=V\) and \(B=C=\varnothing\), the population-storage predicate in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}source\text{-}bridge\text{-}moves}\) is exactly \(V\perp\!\!\!\perp S\). Saturation therefore makes the corresponding population key present, unless it is already present, and preserves its annotation. The storage invariant then gives
\[
 q_S(v)=P_M(V=v\mid S=1)=P_M(V=v),
 \tag{4}
\]
where conditioning is defined because \(P_M(S=1)>0\). Thus the same full-population scalar keys are available with the claimed annotations.

Now let \(T_0=\varnothing\). Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) says that the unique trivial margin contributes no scalar key. A margin-extension instance requires a nonempty population-margin input key, so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}source\text{-}bridge\text{-}moves}\) makes no such instance admissible. Initially every present key is selected-tagged. Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}graphical\text{-}fixing\text{-}moves}\) preserve source tags. The only source-changing moves are margin extension and population storage; the former is unavailable, while the latter maps
\[
 (A,B,C,\mathrm{sel},a,b,c)
 \longmapsto
 (A,B,C,\mathrm{pop},a,b,c)
 \tag{5}
\]
with unchanged annotation exactly when
\[
 A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C
 \quad\text{in }G_{\overline B}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Induction on the number of transitions shows that every selected key belongs to the closure of selected initialization under selected probability and graphical-fixing moves, and that every population key is either an output (5) satisfying (6) or follows from such outputs by population probability and graphical-fixing moves. Conversely, any absent output in these closures whose complete inputs are present remains enabled. Finiteness and the preceding no-permanent-postponement argument show that saturation adds it before termination. Hence the resulting closure has exactly the asserted keys. Setting \(B=C=\varnothing\) in (6) gives unconditional selection independence.

Finally, suppose margin extension reconstructs every cell of the full population law. Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}margin\text{-}extension}\) gives, at each reconstructed cell \((t,z)\),
\[
 P_M(T_0=t,Z=z)
 =P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t,S=1)q_0(t),
 \tag{7}
\]
and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}extid\text{-}storage\text{-}invariant}\) says that the transition annotation is the right-hand side of (7). Taking \(Z=V\setminus T_0\), or composing reconstructed population blocks by the probability moves, makes every key
\[
 (V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},v,\ast,\ast)
\]
present with annotation \(P_M(V=v)\). The replay argument leading to (3) now applies. In particular, under an adjustment criterion with adjustment block \(L\), it returns
\[
 P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
 =\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal X_L}
 P_M(Y=y\mid X=x,L=\ell)P_M(L=\ell),
 \tag{8}
\]
and under the corresponding front-door criterion with mediating block \(D\), it returns
\[
 P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
 =\sum_{d\in\mathcal X_D}P_M(D=d\mid X=x)
 \sum_{x'\in\mathcal X_X}
 P_M(Y=y\mid D=d,X=x')P_M(X=x').
 \tag{9}
\]
The named graphical criteria are precisely the premises making the usual do-calculus derivations of (8)--(9) legal; Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}rules}\) validates each graphical equality, and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\) realizes the finite sums, products, and positive divisions.

Apply (3) to every successful \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\). Each returned coordinate equals its coordinate of \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)\) throughout the exact fiber. If all runs succeed, Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}kernel\text{-}collection}\) forms \(\mathbf F\) in the same order, so
\[
 \mathbf F(q_S,q_0)
 =\bigl(F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0):(x,y)\in\mathcal I\bigr)^{\mathsf T}
 =\bigl(\psi_{x,y}(M):(x,y)\in\mathcal I\bigr)^{\mathsf T}
 =\boldsymbol\psi(M).
\]
If some run fails, \(\mathbf F\) is not formed, while the proved coordinatewise equality remains valid for every returned cell. This proves all four reductions and the collection claim.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathcal G\) be an arbitrary finite selection ADMG on \(V\cup\{S\}\), and put \(G_V=\mathcal G[V]\). Fix \(T_0\subseteq V\) and \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\). Suppose \(\psi_{x,y}\) is not identifiable from the full observational law \(P(V)\) over the positive finite recursive semi-Markovian substantive SCMs compatible with \(G_V\). Then there exist two such substantive models \(N_1,N_2\) and a strictly positive common table \(p\) such that
\[
 P_{N_1}(V=v)=P_{N_2}(V=v)=p(v)>0
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(N_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(N_2).
\]
For any common strictly positive table \(\pi_S(1\mid r)\in(0,1)\), indexed by cells \(r\) of \(\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)\), there are edge-silent extensions \(M_1,M_2\) compatible with the full graph \(\mathcal G\): the equation for \(S\) realizes \(\pi_S\) using an independent finite response coordinate and ignores every exogenous coordinate displayed by a bidirected edge incident to \(S\); every substantive equation retains its equation from \(N_k\), ignores a displayed parent \(S\), and ignores every exogenous coordinate displayed by a bidirected edge incident to \(S\). Define
\[
 q_S(v)=
 \frac{\pi_S(1\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v)}
 {\sum_{v'}\pi_S(1\mid v'_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v')},
 \qquad
 q_0(t)=\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}p(v).
\]
For every \(\epsilon\) satisfying \(0<\epsilon\leq\min_v q_S(v)\),
\[
 (q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0),
 \qquad
 M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0),
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_1)=\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_2)=(q_S,q_0),
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M_2).
\]
The two extensions admit finite independent response representations such that, after zero-mass response labels are deleted, every active atom in either representation has mass at least one common witness-specific constant \(\eta>0\). Consequently ordinary positive-model nonidentifiability implies two-law nonidentifiability over the full positive \(\mathcal G\)-compatible model class for every \(T_0\), because the edge-silent extensions form a subclass of that class.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(G_V=\mathcal G[V]\). Semantic nonidentifiability means that the query is not constant on at least one fiber of the full observational-law map. The positive finite separating pair is supplied by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}kivva\text{-}positive\text{-}ordinary\text{-}id\text{-}specialization}\), which gives substantive models \(N_1,N_2\) compatible with \(G_V\) and a table \(p\) satisfying
\[
 P_{N_1}(V=v)=P_{N_2}(V=v)=p(v)>0
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
 \tag{1}
\]
and
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(N_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(N_2).
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus the cited positive ordinary-identification result is used only for (1)--(2). By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\text{-}response\text{-}selection\text{-}admg\text{-}reduction}\), we may choose finite independent response representations of \(N_1,N_2\) preserving their complete factual and counterfactual laws. Delete zero-mass response labels; hence every remaining coordinate atom has positive mass.

We next construct the extensions rather than assuming their existence. Let
\[
 \mathcal H_S
 =\bigl\{g:\mathcal X_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}\bigr\}.
\]
This is finite by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}state}\). Introduce an exogenous coordinate \(U_S\), independent of all substantive coordinates, with
\[
 P(U_S=g)
 =\prod_{r\in\mathcal X_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)}}
 \pi_S(1\mid r)^{g(r)}
 \{1-\pi_S(1\mid r)\}^{1-g(r)}.
 \tag{3}
\]
The empty-parent case uses the unique empty-block cell. Repeated finite distributivity gives
\[
 \sum_{g\in\mathcal H_S}P(U_S=g)
 =\prod_r\{\pi_S(1\mid r)+1-\pi_S(1\mid r)\}=1.
\]
Every factor in (3) is strictly positive, so every atom of \(U_S\) has positive mass. Define
\[
 S=U_S\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)\bigr).
 \tag{4}
\]
For every bidirected edge incident to \(S\), take its displayed shared exogenous coordinate to have one atom of mass one and make both incident structural equations ignore that coordinate. For every \(W\in V\), retain the substantive equation from \(N_k\); if \(S\) is a displayed parent of \(W\), extend the equation constantly in its \(S\)-argument. Thus every substantive equation also ignores the coordinates displayed by bidirected edges incident to \(S\).

We verify compatibility explicitly. Under the nonparametric ADMG convention in Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}semi\text{-}markovian}\), a structural function may depend only on displayed directed parents and its allowed exogenous coordinates; it is not required to depend nontrivially on every displayed argument. Indeed, if \(f(d,u)\) is an allowed function of a subset of displayed arguments, then \(\widetilde f(d,e,u)=f(d,u)\) is a function on the full displayed argument space, constant in the unused coordinate \(e\). Such constant extension introduces no unauthorized directed or bidirected dependence. The equations just constructed therefore use only arguments permitted by \(\mathcal G\). Their exogenous coordinates are independent, and each shared coordinate is incident to at most its displayed pair. Finally, the directed part of \(\mathcal G\) is acyclic, so evaluating these equations in a topological order is recursive even when \(S\) is not terminal. Hence each \(M_k\) is recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with the full arbitrary graph \(\mathcal G\).

Because every substantive equation ignores \(S\), \(U_S\), and every \(S\)-incident shared coordinate, the factual vector \(V\) is exactly the factual vector generated by \(N_k\). The same observation holds after any intervention on a subset of \(V\). Therefore (1)--(2) imply
\[
 P_{M_k}(V=v)=p(v),
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(M_k)=\psi_{x,y}(N_k),
 \quad k\in\{1,2\},
 \tag{5}
\]
and in particular
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M_2).
 \tag{6}
\]
This is the step that removes the former terminality and selection-unconfoundedness restrictions.

Equation (3) also makes \(U_S\) independent of \(V\). For a fixed parent cell \(r\), summing (3) over all response maps with \(g(r)=1\) gives
\[
 P\{U_S(r)=1\}
 =\pi_S(1\mid r)
 \prod_{r'\ne r}\{\pi_S(1\mid r')+1-\pi_S(1\mid r')\}
 =\pi_S(1\mid r).
 \tag{7}
\]
Consequently, for every substantive cell \(v\), (4), (5), and (7) give
\[
 P_{M_k}(V=v,S=1)
 =\pi_S(1\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v).
 \tag{8}
\]
Let
\[
 Z_S=\sum_{v'}\pi_S(1\mid v'_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v').
\]
All summands are strictly positive, and there are finitely many cells, so \(0<Z_S<\infty\). Summing (8) yields \(P_{M_k}(S=1)=Z_S\). Division is therefore licensed, and
\[
 P_{M_k}(V=v\mid S=1)
 =\frac{\pi_S(1\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v)}{Z_S}
 =q_S(v).
 \tag{9}
\]
The right-hand side is common to the two models, sums to one, and is strictly positive at every cell. Marginalizing (5) gives, for every \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\),
\[
 P_{M_k}(T_0=t)
 =\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}p(v)
 =q_0(t).
 \tag{10}
\]
Equations (9)--(10) and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\) show
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_1)
 =\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_2)
 =(q_S,q_0).
 \tag{11}
\]

Finiteness and cellwise strict positivity imply \(\min_vq_S(v)>0\). Fix \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\leq\min_vq_S(v)\). The compatibility proved above, \(P_{M_k}(S=1)=Z_S>0\), and (9) put \(M_k\) in \(\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G)\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\). Equation (11) and Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}input\text{-}image}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}observed\text{-}fiber}\) then give
\[
 (q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0),
 \qquad
 M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0).
 \tag{12}
\]

It remains to check the response-interior conclusion. The reduced representations of \(N_1,N_2\) have finitely many active coordinate atoms of positive mass. The selection coordinate in (3) has finitely many positive atoms, and every ignored \(S\)-incident coordinate has its single atom of mass one. Hence the union of the active coordinate-atom masses across both extensions is a finite nonempty set of positive real numbers. Its minimum
\[
 \eta
 =\min\{\text{active coordinate-atom masses in either extension}\}
 >0
 \tag{13}
\]
is a common witness-specific slack. Equations (6), (11), and (12) exhibit two members of one exact two-law fiber with different query values. Because these edge-silent models are members of, hence a subclass of, the full positive \(\mathcal G\)-compatible class, a functional valid on that superclass would have to take one value on their common input, contradicting (6). This monotonic superclass argument proves two-law nonidentifiability. It does not assert the invalid reverse implication that identification on the edge-silent subclass would establish identification on the full superclass.
added_lemmas.justification: This all-graph edge-silent lift proves that ordinary positive-model nonidentifiability survives the selected conditional and every external margin inside the full graph-compatible superclass.
added_lemmas.gap: The ordinary positive witness supplies a common full law; the new construction activates no displayed edge at selection, proves full-graph compatibility, preserves the normalized selected law and every margin exactly, and retains query separation.
added_lemmas.consumer: It is the graph-level necessary obstruction for every external-margin recovery claim and the necessary half of the terminal full-margin equivalence.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathcal G\) be any finite selection ADMG on \(V\cup\{S\}\), put \(G_V=\mathcal G[V]\), fix \(T_0\subseteq V\), and fix \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\). If \(\psi_{x,y}\) is identifiable from \((P_M(V\mid S=1),P_M(T_0))\) over the full class of positive finite recursive semi-Markovian models compatible with \(\mathcal G\), then \(\psi_{x,y}\) is identifiable from \(P_N(V)\) over the positive finite substantive model class compatible with \(G_V\). If \(S\) is terminal and \(T_0=V\), the converse also holds, without any restriction on bidirected edges incident to \(S\); hence on that boundary the two identification statements are equivalent. Moreover, for every \(\epsilon>0\), every compatible input \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,V)\), and every ordinarily identifiable cell, \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) returns a finite arithmetic expression \(F_{x,y}\in\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\) satisfying
\[
 F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M)
\]
for every \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,V;q_S,q_0)\). No converse from a bare \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We prove the necessary direction by contraposition. Suppose \(\psi_{x,y}\) is not identifiable from \(P_N(V)\) over the positive finite substantive model class compatible with \(G_V\). Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}all\text{-}graph\text{-}positive\text{-}ordinary\text{-}selection\text{-}lift}\) supplies edge-silent models \(M_1,M_2\) compatible with the full arbitrary graph \(\mathcal G\) such that
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_1)=\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_2)
 \quad\text{but}\quad
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M_2).
 \tag{1}
\]
Their selected tables are strictly positive, so both belong to the full positive graph-compatible model class. If a single two-law identifying map existed on that full class, applying it to the common left-hand input in (1) would force the two right-hand query values to be equal. This contradiction proves the contrapositive. The reasoning uses a separating subclass to refute identification on its superclass; it makes no reverse claim from subclass identification.

Now suppose \(S\) is terminal and \(T_0=V\). The necessary implication just proved does not require terminality. For the converse, assume ordinary identification on \(G_V\), and let \(f\) be its identifying map, so
\[
 f(P_N(V))=\psi_{x,y}(N)
 \tag{2}
\]
for every positive finite substantive model \(N\) compatible with \(G_V\). Take any positive finite model \(M\) compatible with \(\mathcal G\). Delete the equation for \(S\) and retain all substantive equations and exogenous coordinates. Terminality means that \(S\) is not a directed parent of any substantive vertex, so no retained equation uses \(S\). A coordinate represented by a bidirected edge \(S\leftrightarrow W\) can remain as a private disturbance of \(W\) after \(S\) is deleted; it is independent of the other exogenous coordinates and affects at most that one retained equation. Thus the retained system, denoted \(N_M\), is recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with \(G_V\), even when bidirected edges are incident to \(S\). Deletion changes neither the factual law on \(V\) nor any intervention on \(V\), whence
\[
 P_{N_M}(V)=P_M(V),
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(N_M)=\psi_{x,y}(M).
 \tag{3}
\]

The ordinary positivity premise required in (2) follows from selected positivity rather than being added silently. If \(P_M(S=1)>0\) and \(P_M(V=v\mid S=1)>0\), then
\[
 P_M(V=v)
 \geq P_M(V=v,S=1)
 =P_M(S=1)P_M(V=v\mid S=1)>0
 \tag{4}
\]
for every \(v\). Because \(T_0=V\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\) gives \(q_0=P_M(V)\). Combining (2)--(4), the explicit two-law map
\[
 F(q_S,q_0)=f(q_0)
 \tag{5}
\]
satisfies \(F(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M)\) for every positive model compatible with \(\mathcal G\). This proves the converse and the exact terminal full-margin equivalence without excluding incident bidirected edges.

For the executable claim, fix \(\epsilon>0\) and \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,V)\). Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}ordinary\text{-}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}completeness}\) provides a finite ordinary do-calculus and probability derivation of every ordinarily identifiable cell from \(q_0=P(V)\) on \(G_V\). When selection is terminal and the external margin is the entire \(P(V)\), deletion of selection preserves the substantive model even with incident bidirected edges, so the diagnostic becomes an equivalence and EXT-ID is executable. prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The edge-silent theorem proves only a necessary transfer from ordinary positive-model nonidentifiability and does not characterize all information contributed by a selected law and a proper external margin. It uses a compatible subclass in which displayed selection-adjacent arguments are inactive; the reverse direction from identification on this subclass to the full compatible superclass is invalid and is not claimed. EXT-ID soundness and termination do not imply that \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) yields a separating exact-fiber pair. Universal two-law completeness, the margin-anchored hedge, and the parameterized three-node real-closed-field elimination remain unresolved, and no QE3 execution is reported. prose_updates.honest_scope: Termination holds for every syntactically valid cell input; soundness and boundary claims hold on the compatible image \(\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\) and its exact fibers. The all-graph theorem gives a witness-specific \(\epsilon>0\) and response-atom slack \(\eta>0\); it proves that ordinary positive-model failure implies failure over the full two-law graph-compatible superclass for every \(T_0\). It does not prove the converse for a proper margin, does not certify any bare EXT-ID failure, and does not establish universal two-law completeness. Exact equivalence and guaranteed EXT-ID replay are claimed only when \(S\) is terminal and \(T_0=V\), although bidirected edges may be incident to \(S\). Do-search has no failure-completeness theorem for unrestricted Row 8, and Qiu et al.'s result remains a disjoint-support input-shape and scalar-estimand analogue under its published continuous probability-class setup. If \(\psi_{x,y}\) is identifiable from \((P_M(V\mid S=1),P_M(T_0))\) over the full class of positive finite recursive semi-Markovian models compatible with \(\mathcal G\), then \(\psi_{x,y}\) is identifiable from \(P_N(V)\) over the positive finite substantive model class compatible with \(G_V\). If \(S\) is terminal and \(T_0=V\), the converse also holds, without any restriction on bidirected edges incident to \(S\); hence on that boundary the two identification statements are equivalent. Moreover, for every \(\epsilon>0\), every compatible input \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,V)\), and every ordinarily identifiable cell, \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) returns a finite arithmetic expression \(F_{x,y}\in\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\) satisfying
\[
 F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M)
\]
for every \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,V;q_S,q_0)\). No converse from a bare \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) is asserted.
payload.proof_tex:
We prove the necessary direction by contraposition. Suppose \(\psi_{x,y}\) is not identifiable from \(P_N(V)\) over the positive finite substantive model class compatible with \(G_V\). Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}all\text{-}graph\text{-}positive\text{-}ordinary\text{-}selection\text{-}lift}\) supplies edge-silent models \(M_1,M_2\) compatible with the full arbitrary graph \(\mathcal G\) such that
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_1)=\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_2)
 \quad\text{but}\quad
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M_2).
 \tag{1}
\]
Their selected tables are strictly positive, so both belong to the full positive graph-compatible model class. If a single two-law identifying map existed on that full class, applying it to the common left-hand input in (1) would force the two right-hand query values to be equal. This contradiction proves the contrapositive. The reasoning uses a separating subclass to refute identification on its superclass; it makes no reverse claim from subclass identification.

Now suppose \(S\) is terminal and \(T_0=V\). The necessary implication just proved does not require terminality. For the converse, assume ordinary identification on \(G_V\), and let \(f\) be its identifying map, so
\[
 f(P_N(V))=\psi_{x,y}(N)
 \tag{2}
\]
for every positive finite substantive model \(N\) compatible with \(G_V\). Take any positive finite model \(M\) compatible with \(\mathcal G\). Delete the equation for \(S\) and retain all substantive equations and exogenous coordinates. Terminality means that \(S\) is not a directed parent of any substantive vertex, so no retained equation uses \(S\). A coordinate represented by a bidirected edge \(S\leftrightarrow W\) can remain as a private disturbance of \(W\) after \(S\) is deleted; it is independent of the other exogenous coordinates and affects at most that one retained equation. Thus the retained system, denoted \(N_M\), is recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with \(G_V\), even when bidirected edges are incident to \(S\). Deletion changes neither the factual law on \(V\) nor any intervention on \(V\), whence
\[
 P_{N_M}(V)=P_M(V),
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(N_M)=\psi_{x,y}(M).
 \tag{3}
\]

The ordinary positivity premise required in (2) follows from selected positivity rather than being added silently. If \(P_M(S=1)>0\) and \(P_M(V=v\mid S=1)>0\), then
\[
 P_M(V=v)
 \geq P_M(V=v,S=1)
 =P_M(S=1)P_M(V=v\mid S=1)>0
 \tag{4}
\]
for every \(v\). Because \(T_0=V\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\) gives \(q_0=P_M(V)\). Combining (2)--(4), the explicit two-law map
\[
 F(q_S,q_0)=f(q_0)
 \tag{5}
\]
satisfies \(F(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M)\) for every positive model compatible with \(\mathcal G\). This proves the converse and the exact terminal full-margin equivalence without excluding incident bidirected edges.

For the executable claim, fix \(\epsilon>0\) and \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,V)\). Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}ordinary\text{-}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}completeness}\) provides a finite ordinary do-calculus and probability derivation of every ordinarily identifiable cell from \(q_0=P(V)\) on \(G_V\). Its graphical separation predicates remain valid in \(\mathcal G\): every path between substantive vertices that is absent from \(G_V\) but present in \(\mathcal G\) must pass through \(S\); because \(S\) is terminal, both incident edges have arrowheads at \(S\), and \(S\) has no directed descendant. Thus \(S\) is an unconditioned collider with no conditioned descendant in every relevant mutilated graph, since the conditioning blocks are subsets of \(V\). Such a path is blocked. Hence the ordinary derivation is a legal population-tagged derivation in the transition system.

Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}boundary\text{-}reductions}\) now applies: full-margin initialization stores every cell of \(q_0=P(V)\), and saturation replays that finite derivation. It returns some \(F_{x,y}\in\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\). Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}extid\text{-}sound\text{-}termination}\) then yields, for every \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,V;q_S,q_0)\),
\[
 F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M).
 \tag{6}
\]
This argument proves success only on the terminal full-margin boundary for ordinarily identifiable cells and does not turn \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) into a general nonidentification certificate.
