carrier.proof_tex:
Let \(C_Q\), \(D\), and \(R\) denote, respectively, the covariate block, binary treatment, and outcome in \(\mathrm{lem{:}qiu\text{-}external\text{-}ate\text{-}characterization}\). Relabel the variables for the purpose of comparing signatures by
\[
T_0=C_Q,\qquad X=\{D\},\qquad Y=\{R\},\qquad
V=C_Q\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{D,R\}.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\), the two entries of the present observation map under (1) are
\[
\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M)
=\bigl(P_M(V\mid S=1),P_M(T_0)\bigr)
=\bigl(P_M(C_Q,D,R\mid S=1),P_M(C_Q)\bigr).
\tag{2}
\]
The cited lemma states that Qiu et al. use a selected observational law together with an external unbiased covariate margin. Thus (2) proves equality of the two data-slot patterns after relabeling. It does not assert equality, inclusion, or even nonempty intersection of the two model classes.

We next verify the estimand map. Suppose only for this calculation that \(R\) has a finite numeric state space and \(D\) is binary. Every sum below is finite, so no integrability or limiting condition is needed. The definitions of \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\) and \(\psi_{x,y}\) give, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(M)
&=E_M[R\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1)]
  -E_M[R\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0)]\\
&=\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,
  P_M(R=r\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1))
  -\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,
  P_M(R=r\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0))\\
&=\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,\psi_{1,r}(M)
  -\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,\psi_{0,r}(M).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
Hence the finite table \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)\), whose coordinatewise role is made explicit in \(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}kernel\text{-}collection}\), determines \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(M)\) through the displayed linear map.

The converse to this last implication fails inside a strictly positive finite Markovian DAG subclass. Consider the graph \(D\to R\) with \(S\) isolated, take \(X=\{D\}\), \(Y=\{R\}\), and let \(T_0=\varnothing\). Let \(U_D\) and \(U_S\) be independent Bernoulli\((1/2)\) variables, and let \(U_R\) be independent of them and uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,12\}\). In model \(M_j\), set
\[
D=U_D,\qquad S=U_S,
\qquad
R_1=\mathbf 1\{U_R\le 3+6D\},
\qquad
R_2=\mathbf 1\{U_R\le 4+6D\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Each model is finite and recursive. Its exogenous variables are mutually independent, so it is Markovian and therefore semi-Markovian; its structural equations follow the displayed DAG. Also \(P_{M_j}(S=1)=1/2>0\). Independence of \(S\) from \((D,R_j)\) yields the selected cell tables
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
&(D,R_j)=(0,1)&(0,0)&(1,1)&(1,0)\\ \hline
j=1&1/8&3/8&3/8&1/8\\
j=2&1/6&1/3&5/12&1/12.
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Every cell in (5) is positive; in fact both models satisfy the selected-cell lower bound \(1/12\). Thus the positivity assertion uses no boundary point. Intervention replaces the equation \(D=U_D\) and leaves the equation for \(R_j\) unchanged, so (4) gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc|c}
&P_{M_j}(R=1\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0))
&P_{M_j}(R=1\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1))
&\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(M_j)\\ \hline
j=1&3/12&9/12&6/12\\
j=2&4/12&10/12&6/12.
\end{array}
\tag{6}
\]
Both scalar effects equal \(1/2\), while \(\psi_{0,1}(M_1)=1/4\ne1/3=\psi_{0,1}(M_2)\). Therefore the linear map in (3) is not injective even on the stated positive finite DAG subclass: identification of the scalar effect alone cannot decide every coordinate of \(\boldsymbol\psi\).

It remains to establish the two scope separations. By \(\mathrm{lem{:}qiu\text{-}external\text{-}ate\text{-}characterization}\), Qiu et al.'s theorem assumes unconfoundedness, treatment overlap on the covariate support, and a pairwise distinguishability condition on specified classes of propensity, covariate--potential-outcome, and selection laws. Its conclusion identifies the single scalar \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\), not every cell \(\psi_{x,y}\) for arbitrary semi-Markovian \(\mathcal G\). Equation (6) additionally shows why the scalar conclusion cannot be inverted into the full-table conclusion. Thus the cited theorem does not subsume the present arbitrary-cell graph problem.

Conversely, \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\) restricts the present class to finite-state recursive semi-Markovian models and imposes only the listed graph, selection, and selected-cell positivity conditions. The cited lemma states both that Qiu et al.'s exposition includes continuous covariate--outcome laws with densities and that its identification criterion is indexed by separately specified probability classes. Continuous-law examples are not members of the present finite-state class. Moreover, a graph \(\mathcal G\) and the membership conditions in \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\) do not supply a chosen triple of probability classes or assert Qiu et al.'s pairwise distinguishability condition. Hence the present graph class does not subsume the cited setup. Together with (2), (3), and (6), these observations prove precisely an input-shape and estimand-map analogy, the failure of the reverse estimand map, and non-subsumption in both directions, without claiming a literal model-class intersection.

The theorem's conclusion concerns that scalar average treatment effect, not every cell of an interventional outcome distribution or the complete interventional table. Their setup assumes continuous covariate--outcome laws with densities for exposition and includes continuous probability-family examples.

semantic_closure.statement: Every recursive semi-Markovian SCM compatible with a finite-state selection ADMG \(\mathcal G\) has, with respect to the full joint law of all factual and counterfactual variables on \(V\cup\{S\}\), an equivalent graph-compatible representation with finitely many independent exogenous coordinates of finite cardinality.  The representation can be written using a finite graph- and state-space-determined inventory of deterministic response maps and a product of finite coordinate-weight simplices.  It preserves \(P_M(V,S)\), every margin \(P_M(T_0)\), and every intervention cell \(\psi_{x,y}(M)\); when \(P_M(S=1)>0\), it therefore also preserves \(q_S^M=P_M(V\mid S=1)\).

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
By the meaning of recursive semi-Markovian compatibility in \(\mathrm{ass{:}semi\text{-}markovian}\), expand \(\mathcal G\) to its canonical latent DAG \(\widetilde{\mathcal G}\): the main variables are \(V\cup\{S\}\), every disturbance is exogenous, and the independent disturbance coordinates encode exactly the bidirected and private exogenous inputs permitted by \(\mathcal G\).  This expansion is merely the defining latent-DAG realization of the ADMG and changes no structural equation or counterfactual variable.

The main-variable state spaces are finite by \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}state}\).  Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\text{-}disturbance\text{-}full\text{-}law\text{-}reduction}\) to \(\widetilde{\mathcal G}\).  It replaces every disturbance cardinality by a sufficiently large finite one without changing the full data law.  In particular, it preserves the joint factual law \(P_M(V,S)\), the marginal \(P_M(T_0)\), and the joint law of every counterfactual outcome under \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\), hence preserves \(\psi_{x,y}(M)\).

For each finite disturbance coordinate, two atom labels that induce the same deterministic response map at all of their graph-permitted children can be merged.  Because every observed parent configuration and every child state space is finite, there are only finitely many such response maps.  After merging, the independent disturbance law remains a product of finite coordinate-weight vectors, and the acyclic structural recursion is a deterministic function of their joint assignment.  Enumerating the finitely many nonempty support subsets of these finite response-map sets gives the claimed finite inventory of support strata.  Finally, if \(P_M(S=1)>0\), equality of \(P_M(V,S)\) gives
\[
 P_M(V=v\mid S=1)=\frac{P_M(V=v,S=1)}{\sum_{v'}P_M(V=v',S=1)},
\]
with a common positive denominator, so the selected conditional is preserved as well.  This proves the adaptation.

semantic_closure.statement:

If an intervention cell \(P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\) is not identifiable from \(P(V)\) over the positive finite recursive semi-Markovian model class, then there exist two positive finite recursive semi-Markovian SCMs \(N_1,N_2\) compatible with the same substantive graph and a probability table \(p\) such that
\[
 P_{N_1}(V=v)=P_{N_2}(V=v)=p(v)>0
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
\]
but
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(N_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(N_2).
\]

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(\epsilon>0\), \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), and \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\).  The scalar causal query is not point identified on the exact observed-data fiber if and only if the canonical response-fiber formula is feasible:
\[
 \bigl[\exists M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0):
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)\neq\psi_{x,y}(M_2)\bigr]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{RF}_{x,y}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0).
\]
Whenever the right-hand side is feasible, its two response points themselves construct finite graph-compatible witnesses with positive selection normalizers, exact selected-law cross-products, exact external-margin rows, and active atom masses bounded below by the displayed common witness-specific \(\eta>0\).  Conversely every finite separating pair in the exact fiber supplies such a feasible response-point pair after zero-mass response labels are deleted.  Hence exact-fiber nonidentification has the displayed computable finite semialgebraic witness characterization, but no implication from a terminal \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) failure to feasibility of this formula is asserted.
semantic_closure.justification: This gives an exact, finite, computable witness formula for nonidentification on a fixed two-law fiber without claiming that EXT-ID failure makes the formula feasible.
semantic_closure.gap: Existing response-function encodings do not spell out the normalized selected-law cross-products, independent margin rows, common positive-support slack, and unequal intervention cell in one exact-fiber criterion.
semantic_closure.consumer: An ACTG 320 margin audit can use a feasible response pair as a rigorous insufficiency certificate even when no universal graph-only failure extractor is available.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
First suppose \(\operatorname{RF}_{x,y}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\) is feasible.  For \(i=1,2\), use the deterministic response maps in the selected stratum and the independent coordinate laws \(w^{(i)}_{\ell j}\) to construct the recursive SCM \(M_i\).  The stratum contains only response maps allowed by \(\mathcal G\), so \(M_i\) is graph compatible and semi-Markovian.  Its exogenous law is the product law, and the law of total probability over \(\omega\) gives, directly from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}canonical\text{-}response\text{-}fiber\text{-}formula}\),
\[
 P_{M_i}(V=v,S=1)=p_{\vartheta^{(i)}}(v,1),
 \quad
 P_{M_i}(T_0=t)=m_{\vartheta^{(i)}}(t),
 \quad
 P_{M_i}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))=g_{\vartheta^{(i)},x,y}.
\]
Also
\[
 P_{M_i}(S=1)=\sum_vp_{\vartheta^{(i)}}(v,1)
 =\rho_{\vartheta^{(i)}}>0.
\]
The selected-law equations in the formula therefore imply
\[
 P_{M_i}(V=v\mid S=1)
 =\frac{p_{\vartheta^{(i)}}(v,1)}{\rho_{\vartheta^{(i)}}}
 =q_S(v)
\]
for every \(v\); division is licensed by \(\rho_{\vartheta^{(i)}}>0\).  The margin equations similarly give \(P_{M_i}(T_0=t)=q_0(t)\) for every \(t\).  Since the fixed input satisfies \(q_S(v)\geq\epsilon\), each \(M_i\) belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G)\), and hence to \(\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\).  Finally,
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)-\psi_{x,y}(M_2)
 =g_{\vartheta^{(1)},x,y}-g_{\vartheta^{(2)},x,y}\neq0.
\]
The inequalities \(w^{(i)}_{\ell j}\geq\eta>0\) give the claimed common interior slack on the exact active supports.

Conversely, suppose finite models \(M_1,M_2\) in the exact fiber separate the query.  Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\text{-}response\text{-}selection\text{-}admg\text{-}reduction}\) to each model, preserving its full factual and counterfactual law.  Record the resulting deterministic response map taken by every atom of each independent finite exogenous coordinate.  Merge atoms that induce the same response label, and delete every label of mass zero.  This produces a canonical active-support stratum and strictly positive coordinate weights \(w^{(i)}_{\ell j}\) without changing any structural response, observational probability, margin probability, or intervention probability.  Since the pair has finitely many active weights, the number
\[
 \eta=\min_{i,\ell,j}w^{(i)}_{\ell j}
\]
exists and is strictly positive.  Let \(\vartheta^{(i)}\) be the resulting response point and \(\rho_i=P_{M_i}(S=1)>0\).  Membership in the exact fiber gives, cell by cell,
\[
 p_{\vartheta^{(i)}}(v,1)
 =P_{M_i}(V=v,S=1)
 =q_S(v)P_{M_i}(S=1)
 =q_S(v)\rho_i,
\]
\[
 m_{\vartheta^{(i)}}(t)=P_{M_i}(T_0=t)=q_0(t),
 \qquad
 g_{\vartheta^{(i)},x,y}=\psi_{x,y}(M_i).
\]
The last two values differ by hypothesis, so every clause of \(\operatorname{RF}_{x,y}\) holds.

Finally, the graph admits only finitely many deterministic response maps and active-support strata.  Within each stratum, the displayed probabilities are finite sums of monomials in the coordinate weights; normalization, common-interior, positive-normalizer, exact-fiber, and query-separation requirements are polynomial equalities or strict or weak polynomial inequalities.  Thus the disjunction is a finite semialgebraic feasibility problem whose variables and constraints are written explicitly in the definition.  This establishes both directions and the computable witness characterization.

semantic_closure.statement: For every finite syntactically valid cell input \((\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0,q_S,q_0)\), \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) terminates with at most \(\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert\le2\{(1+3r)^{\lvert V\rvert}-(1+2r)^{\lvert V\rvert}\}\) scalar keys ever present: every nonterminal transition adds one previously absent scalar key and strictly decreases \(\mu(\sigma)\). Every legal move instance belongs to the finite universe \(\mathscr U\), and its output remains in \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\). Fix \(\epsilon>0\) and require \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\). If the procedure returns \(F_{x,y}\in\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\), then \[F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M)=P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\] for every \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\). Running the procedure over every \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\) therefore yields \(\mathbf F(q_S,q_0)=\boldsymbol\psi(M)\) for every model in that exact fiber whenever all cell runs succeed.
semantic_closure.justification: The bounded canonical key inventory makes both validity of every successful expression and termination independently auditable.
semantic_closure.gap: Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim prove IDSB sound; this claim gives an exact finite transition system, source-tag invariant, and graph-indexed termination measure for saturation over the same two observed laws, without claiming failure completeness.
semantic_closure.consumer: Every successful ACTG audit formula comes with a finite derivation trace that can be checked against the selected table and audited margin.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Write \(d_W=\lvert\mathcal X_W\rvert\leq r\) for each \(W\in V\).  To specify a scalar key, each vertex is either absent, assigned to \(A\) with one of \(d_W\) cell values, assigned to \(B\) with one of \(d_W\) values, or assigned to \(C\) with one of \(d_W\) values.  Requiring \(A\neq\varnothing\) subtracts the assignments having no \(A\)-vertex, and the two source tags contribute a factor of two.  Hence Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) and the inventory definition give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert
 &=2\left\{\prod_{W\in V}(1+3d_W)-\prod_{W\in V}(1+2d_W)\right\}\\
 &\leq2\left\{(1+3r)^{\lvert V\rvert}-(1+2r)^{\lvert V\rvert}\right\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first equality is also obtained by partitioning according to the disjoint sets \(A,B,C\) and then counting their cells.

The ordered instance universe \(\mathscr U\) is finite because \(V\), \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and the move-tag set are finite.  Every enabled nonterminal transition is, by definition, an instance in \(\mathscr U\) whose output is a key in \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and the absent-output condition gives
\[
 K_{\sigma'}=K_\sigma\cup\{\xi_{\mathrm{out}}\},
 \qquad \xi_{\mathrm{out}}\notin K_\sigma.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \mu(\sigma')
 =\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\setminus K_{\sigma'}\rvert
 =\mu(\sigma)-1.
\]
The nonnegative integer \(\mu\) can decrease only finitely many times.  Each intervening scan is over the finite ordered set \(\mathscr U\), so a scan either adds such a key, returns a present target, or returns \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  Thus the procedure terminates and never has more than \(\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert\) keys present.

Now fix a compatible input and a model \(M\) in its exact fiber.  By Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}extid\text{-}storage\text{-}invariant}\), every annotation at every reachable state equals the interventional-kernel cell named by its key.  Finite sums and products preserve membership in \(\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\), and a division is performed only when its denominator is positive; induction on the transition count therefore also shows that every annotation is in \(\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\).  If the target key is present, its key is
\[
 (Y,X,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},y,x,\ast),
\]
so its annotation satisfies
\[
 F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)
 =P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
 =\psi_{x,y}(M).
\]
The input tables are common to every \(M\) in the exact fiber, so the same equality holds simultaneously for every such model.  Applying the cell argument in the finite lexicographic order on \(\mathcal I\) and using Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}kernel\text{-}collection}\) gives, whenever all runs succeed,
\[
 \mathbf F(q_S,q_0)=\{\psi_{x,y}(M):(x,y)\in\mathcal I\}
 =\boldsymbol\psi(M)
\]
for every model in the fiber.

semantic_closure.statement:
Let \(S\) be terminal in \(\mathcal G\), suppose no bidirected edge of \(\mathcal G\) is incident to \(S\), and put \(G_V=\mathcal G[V]\). Fix \(T_0\subseteq V\) and a target cell \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\). Suppose \(\psi_{x,y}\) is not identifiable from the full observational law \(P(V)\) over the positive finite recursive semi-Markovian substantive SCMs compatible with \(G_V\). Then there exist two such substantive models \(N_1,N_2\) and a strictly positive common table \(p\) satisfying
\[
 P_{N_1}(V=v)=P_{N_2}(V=v)=p(v)>0\quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(N_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(N_2).
\]
For any common terminal selection kernel \(\pi_S(1\mid r)\in(0,1)\), one value for every cell \(r\) of \(\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)\), implemented by an exogenous response coordinate independent of the substantive coordinates, extend both models by that same kernel and denote the extensions by \(M_1,M_2\). Define
\[
 q_S(v)=\frac{\pi_S(1\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v)}
 {\sum_{v'}\pi_S(1\mid v'_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)})p(v')},
 \qquad
 q_0(t)=\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}p(v).
\]
For every \(\epsilon\) satisfying \(0<\epsilon\leq\min_v q_S(v)\), the pair \((q_S,q_0)\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), both \(M_1,M_2\) belong to the single exact fiber \(\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), and
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_1)=\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_2)=(q_S,q_0),
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M_2).
\]
Moreover the two lifted models admit finite independent response representations such that, after deleting zero-mass response labels, every active atom in either representation has mass at least one common witness-specific constant \(\eta>0\).
semantic_closure.justification: This graph-level transfer shows that positive ordinary nonidentification survives a common terminal-unconfounded selection mechanism and every external margin \(P(T_0)\).
semantic_closure.gap: The cited positive ordinary witness theorem preserves \(P(V)\); the new derivation proves exact preservation of the normalized selected conditional and the unbiased margin in one positive two-law fiber.
semantic_closure.consumer: It yields a necessary condition for recovery from selected data plus any external margin and the converse half of the full-margin boundary equivalence.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 G_V=\mathcal G[V].
\]
The premise is failure of ordinary identification on the positive finite substantive model class. Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}kivva\text{-}positive\text{-}ordinary\text{-}id\text{-}specialization}\), applied to \(G_V\) and the cell \((x,y)\), therefore gives finite recursive semi-Markovian substantive SCMs \(N_1,N_2\) compatible with \(G_V\) and a probability table \(p\) such that, for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\),
\[
 P_{N_1}(V=v)=P_{N_2}(V=v)=p(v)>0,
\]
while
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(N_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(N_2).
\]
This is the only step imported from the cited positive ordinary-identification result.

Fix any terminal selection kernel allowed by the statement and abbreviate
\[
 r_v=\pi_S(1\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(S)}),
 \qquad
 Z=\sum_{v'\in\mathcal X_V}r_{v'}p(v').
\]
Every \(r_v\) and every \(p(v)\) is strictly positive. The state space \(\mathcal X_V\) is finite by \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}state}\), so
\[
 0<Z<\infty.
\]
Because no bidirected edge is incident to \(S\), using an exogenous selection coordinate independent of all substantive exogenous coordinates is compatible with \(\mathcal G\). Because \(S\) is terminal, adjoining its structural equation changes no substantive structural equation and creates no directed feedback. Hence each extension \(M_k\), \(k\in\{1,2\}\), is recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with \(\mathcal G\).

Conditional on \(V=v\), the independent common selection equation has success probability \(r_v\). Thus, for \(k\in\{1,2\}\), the product rule and the common population law give
\[
 P_{M_k}(V=v,S=1)
 =P_{M_k}(S=1\mid V=v)P_{M_k}(V=v)
 =r_vp(v).
\]
Summing this equality over the finite state space yields
\[
 P_{M_k}(S=1)=\sum_v r_vp(v)=Z>0.
\]
Division is therefore licensed, and
\[
 P_{M_k}(V=v\mid S=1)
 =\frac{r_vp(v)}{Z}
 =q_S(v).
\]
The right-hand side does not depend on \(k\). It is a probability table because
\[
 \sum_vq_S(v)=Z^{-1}\sum_vr_vp(v)=1,
\]
and every cell is strictly positive. Likewise marginalization of the common full law gives, for every \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\),
\[
 P_{M_k}(T_0=t)
 =\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}P_{M_k}(V=v)
 =\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}p(v)
 =q_0(t).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_1)
 =\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_2)
 =(q_S,q_0).
\]

Finiteness and strict positivity of the selected table imply
\[
 \min_{v\in\mathcal X_V}q_S(v)>0.
\]
Fix \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\leq\min_vq_S(v)\). The compatibility, positive selection normalizer, and selected-cell inequality established above put each \(M_k\) in \(\mathfrak M_\epsilon(\mathcal G)\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\). Hence the common observed pair lies in \(\mathcal C_\epsilon(\mathcal G,T_0)\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}input\text{-}image}\), and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}observed\text{-}fiber}\) gives
\[
 M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak F_\epsilon(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0).
\]

For an intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\), terminality of \(S\) implies that the selection structural equation is downstream of every substantive variable and is not an input to any substantive equation. The substantive interventional distribution in \(M_k\) is therefore exactly that in \(N_k\). In particular,
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(M_k)=\psi_{x,y}(N_k),\qquad k\in\{1,2\},
\]
so the cited strict inequality yields
\[
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M_2).
\]

It remains to verify, rather than assume, the response-interior assertion. Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\text{-}response\text{-}selection\text{-}admg\text{-}reduction}\) separately to \(M_1\) and \(M_2\). It gives finite independent response representations preserving their full factual laws, the \(T_0\)-margins, and the target intervention cells. In each representation merge response labels inducing the same deterministic maps and delete every zero-mass label. The resulting state space of each coordinate is exactly its positive support. Across the two representations there are only finitely many active coordinate atoms, and every one has strictly positive mass. Therefore
\[
 \eta=\min\{\text{active coordinate-atom masses in either reduced representation}\}>0.
\]
Every active atom in either representation has mass at least \(\eta\), while all equalities already proved are preserved by the reduction. This completes the graph-level positive selection lift.

semantic_closure.statement: For the binary specialization \(V=\{W_\star,A_\star,Y_\star\}\), \(\mathcal G=\mathcal G_\star\), \(X=\{A_\star\}\), \(Y=\{Y_\star\}\), and \(T_0=\{W_\star\}\), the answer to the interior gate is affirmative.  In particular, for \(x=1\), \(y=1\), \(\epsilon=1/16\), the uniform tables \(q_S(w,a,y)=1/8\) and \(q_0(w)=1/2\) form a compatible input at which \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) returns \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  There is a compatible represented baseline \((M,\mathcal R,U_0)\in\mathfrak R_{\epsilon,1/4}^{\circ}(\mathcal G_\star,T_0;q_S,q_0)\) and an active direction \(\beta\in\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}^\perp\) such that \(\beta^{\mathsf T}h_{1,1}=1\).  The perturbations with \(\tau=1/8\) give two models in the same exact fiber with \(P(Y_\star=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_\star=1))=5/8\) and \(3/8\), respectively.
semantic_closure.justification: An explicit four-response-type construction certifies the first nontrivial interior failure gate exactly.
semantic_closure.gap: The construction preserves a normalized selected conditional and an external population margin while changing the intervention cell through one active latent coordinate.
semantic_closure.consumer: This is the required first falsification witness for the universal margin-anchored hedge program.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Let \(U_W\) and \(U_A\) be independent fair binary coordinates, and let \(U_0\) be independent of them with active state space \(\mathcal J_0=\{1,2,3,4\}\) and masses \(u_j=1/4\).  Define
\[
 W_\star=U_W,
 \qquad A_\star=U_A,
\]
and, for \(j\in\mathcal J_0\), define
\[
 f_{Y_\star}(a,j)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&j=1,\\
 1,&j=2,\\
 a,&j=3,\\
 1-a,&j=4.
 \end{cases}
\qquad
 f_S(w,y,j)=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&j\in\{1,2\},\\
 0,&j\in\{3,4\}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Every structural function uses only a subset of its displayed parents in \(\mathcal G_\star\), and the only shared exogenous coordinate is \(U_0\), shared by \(Y_\star\) and \(S\).  Hence the SCM is recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with the directed and bidirected edges of \(\mathcal G_\star\).  Each coordinate state space is exactly its positive support, and every atom has mass at least \(1/4\).

Selection occurs exactly for types \(1,2\), so
\[
 P_M(S=1)=\frac12.
\]
Conditional on selection, \(W_\star\) and \(A_\star\) remain independent fair coins, while types \(1,2\) make \(Y_\star\) respectively \(0,1\) with equal conditional probability.  For every \((w,a,y)\in\{0,1\}^3\), therefore,
\[
 P_M(W_\star=w,A_\star=a,Y_\star=y,S=1)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac14=\frac1{16},
\]
and division by \(P_M(S=1)=1/2\) gives
\[
 q_S(w,a,y)=\frac18.
\]
Also \(q_0(w)=P_M(W_\star=w)=1/2\).  Thus \(q_S(v)\geq1/16\), the input belongs to \(\mathcal C_{1/16}(\mathcal G_\star,T_0)\), and the represented baseline belongs to \(\mathfrak R_{1/16,1/4}^{\circ}(\mathcal G_\star,T_0;q_S,q_0)\).

Order the active types as above and put
\[
 \beta=(0,0,1,-1)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Integrating over the independent fair \(U_W,U_A\) gives
\[
 a_+=(1,1,0,0)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad b_0=b_1=\frac12\mathbf 1.
\]
For a selected full cell with \(y=0\),
\[
 a_v=(1/4,0,0,0)^{\mathsf T},
\]
and for a selected full cell with \(y=1\),
\[
 a_v=(0,1/4,0,0)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Since \(u^{\mathsf T}a_+=1/2\) and \(u^{\mathsf T}a_v=1/16\), every selected cross-product row is a scalar multiple of \((1,-1,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\).  Consequently \(\beta\) is orthogonal to \(\mathbf 1\), each \(b_t\), and every selected cross-product row, and therefore
\[
 \beta\in\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}^\perp.
\]
For \((x,y)=(1,1)\), the intervention-response row is
\[
 h_{1,1}=(0,1,1,0)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \beta^{\mathsf T}h_{1,1}=1.
\]
Thus \(h_{1,1}\notin\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}\).

Take \(\tau=1/8=(1/4)/(2\lVert\beta\rVert_\infty)\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}projective\text{-}nullspace\text{-}certificate}\) applies, with perturbed mass vectors
\[
 u^+=(1/4,1/4,3/8,1/8),
 \qquad
 u^-=(1/4,1/4,1/8,3/8).
\]
They preserve the displayed selected joint law and \(W_\star\)-margin, while direct evaluation gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{M_1}(Y_\star=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_\star=1))
 &=u_2^++u_3^+=\frac58,\\
 P_{M_2}(Y_\star=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_\star=1))
 &=u_2^-+u_3^-=\frac38.
 \end{aligned}
\]
If \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) returned an arithmetic functional at this input, Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}extid\text{-}sound\text{-}termination}\) would force that one value to equal both \(5/8\) and \(3/8\), a contradiction.  The state machine terminates and has only the two terminal outputs specified in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\), so its output here is \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  This proves the claimed exact interior witness.

semantic_closure.statement: Fix \(\epsilon>0\), \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), and \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\). For any \(Z\subseteq V\setminus T_0\) such that \(Z\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid T_0\) in \(\mathcal G\), \[P_M(T_0,Z)=P_M(Z\mid T_0,S=1)q_0(T_0).\]
semantic_closure.justification: This identity is the sound primitive that converts one unbiased margin into a larger population kernel.
semantic_closure.gap: It restates Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim's Lemma 1 as the base case needed by the new recursion.
semantic_closure.consumer: It produces the population kernel used by the ACTG audit whenever the measured margin blocks selection from an additional covariate block.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix a cell \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\) and a cell \(z\in\mathcal X_Z\).  Because \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}observed\text{-}fiber}\) give
\[
 P_M(S=1)>0,\qquad P_M(V=v\mid S=1)=q_S(v)\geq\epsilon
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
\]
and \(P_M(T_0=t)=q_0(t)\).  Summing the selected cells over all full cells whose \(T_0\)-coordinate is \(t\) shows
\[
 P_M(T_0=t\mid S=1)
 =\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}q_S(v)>0.
\]
Consequently \(P_M(T_0=t,S=1)>0\), hence also \(P_M(T_0=t)>0\); every conditional probability used below is therefore defined.

By \(\mathrm{ass{:}semi\text{-}markovian}\), compatibility with \(\mathcal G\) gives the global Markov implication for the stated graphical separation.  Thus \(Z\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid T_0\) in \(\mathcal G\) implies
\[
 P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t,S=1)=P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t).
\]
Multiplication by the positive population margin and then use of the exact-fiber equality yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_M(T_0=t,Z=z)
 &=P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t)P_M(T_0=t)\\
 &=P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t,S=1)q_0(t).
 \end{aligned}
\]
This holds cell by cell.  When \(T_0=\varnothing\), the same calculation uses the unique empty-block cell and the unit margin; when \(Z=\varnothing\), it reduces to the margin identity.  These cover all boundary cases in the statement.

semantic_closure.name: Canonical multi-coordinate exact-fiber witness formula
semantic_closure.construction:
At fixed nonrestrictive finite disturbance cardinalities, a canonical graph-compatible response point \(\vartheta\) selects one of the finitely many active-support strata of deterministic response maps allowed by \(\mathcal G\).  On each of its finitely many independent exogenous coordinates, indexed by \(\ell\), it has a nonempty active set \(\mathcal J_\ell\) and weights \(w_{\ell j}>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_\ell}w_{\ell j}=1\).  For an exogenous assignment \(\omega\in\prod_\ell\mathcal J_\ell\), let the acyclic recursion determine \(V_\vartheta(\omega),S_\vartheta(\omega)\), and the intervened value \(Y_{\vartheta,x}(\omega)\).  Define the explicit multi-affine polynomials
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 p_\vartheta(v,1)
 &=\sum_{\omega:\,V_\vartheta(\omega)=v,\,S_\vartheta(\omega)=1}
      \prod_\ell w_{\ell,\omega_\ell},\\
 m_\vartheta(t)
 &=\sum_{\omega:\,(V_\vartheta(\omega))_{T_0}=t}
      \prod_\ell w_{\ell,\omega_\ell},\\
 g_{\vartheta,x,y}
 &=\sum_{\omega:\,Y_{\vartheta,x}(\omega)=y}
      \prod_\ell w_{\ell,\omega_\ell},
 \qquad
 \rho_\vartheta=\sum_vp_\vartheta(v,1).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The formula \(\operatorname{RF}_{x,y}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\) is the following finite disjunction over ordered pairs of canonical active-support strata: there exist response points \(\vartheta^{(1)},\vartheta^{(2)}\) in the chosen strata and one \(\eta>0\) such that, for \(i=1,2\),
\[
 w^{(i)}_{\ell j}\geq\eta,\qquad
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal J^{(i)}_\ell}w^{(i)}_{\ell j}=1,\qquad
 \rho_{\vartheta^{(i)}}>0,
\]
for every coordinate \(\ell\) and active atom \(j\), and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 p_{\vartheta^{(i)}}(v,1)&=q_S(v)\rho_{\vartheta^{(i)}}
 &&\text{for every }v,\\
 m_{\vartheta^{(i)}}(t)&=q_0(t)
 &&\text{for every }t,\\
 g_{\vartheta^{(1)},x,y}&\neq g_{\vartheta^{(2)},x,y}.&&
 \end{aligned}
\]
All support choices, deterministic response maps, sums, and products in this formula are finite and graph-determined.  Thus \(\operatorname{RF}_{x,y}\) is an explicit finite semialgebraic feasibility formula in the two observed tables; it is a specification of the witness constraints, not an assertion that an exhaustive solver run has been executed.

semantic_closure.name: Finite arithmetic expression language
semantic_closure.construction: For a fixed input \((q_S,q_0)\), \(\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\) is the smallest class of scalar expressions containing every cell of \(q_S\) and \(q_0\) and closed under finite addition, multiplication, and division by an expression whose value at that input is positive. A successful cell run returns one \(F_{x,y}\in\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\); causal validity is asserted only when \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\).

semantic_closure.name: Exact probability-calculus transitions
semantic_closure.construction: For every source tag \(s\), intervention block \(B\), conditioning block \(C\), disjoint nonempty blocks \(A,H\), and fixed output cell, the following are the complete scalar probability-calculus moves. Marginalization requires the \(\lvert\mathcal X_H\rvert\) input keys \(\{(A\cup H,B,C,s,(a,h),b,c):h\in\mathcal X_H\}\), outputs \((A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\), and stores \(E_{\mathrm{out}}=\sum_hE_\sigma(A\cup H,B,C,s,(a,h),b,c)\); it introduces no denominator. Conditioning requires all \(\lvert\mathcal X_A\rvert\) keys \(\{(A\cup H,B,C,s,(a',h),b,c):a'\in\mathcal X_A\}\), outputs \((A,B,C\cup H,s,a,b,(c,h))\), and stores the annotation at \((a,h)\) divided by the sum over \(a'\); it is admissible exactly when that denominator is positive. Chain composition has arity two: inputs \((A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\) and \((H,B,C\cup A,s,h,b,(c,a))\), output \((A\cup H,B,C,s,(a,h),b,c)\), and stored product of the two scalar annotations. The symmetric chain instance interchanges \(A,H\); only the lexicographically first representation of an identical output scalar key is eligible. Each required input and output belongs to \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and each move instance records its complete finite input-key set.

semantic_closure.name: Exact population and selection-aware graphical fixing transitions
semantic_closure.construction: Write \(G_{\overline B}\) for \(\mathcal G\) with arrows into \(B\) removed, \(G_{\overline B,\underline H}\) also with arrows out of \(H\) removed, and \(H_s(C)=H\setminus\operatorname{An}_{G_{\overline B}}(C\cup S_s)\). For \(s\in\{\mathrm{pop},\mathrm{sel}\}\), each scalar transition has arity one, retains its source tag, copies the input annotation, and introduces no denominator. Rule \(1\) maps \((A,B,C\cup H,s,a,b,(c,h))\leftrightarrow(A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\) when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp H\mid B,C,S_s\) in \(G_{\overline B}\). Rule \(2\) maps \((A,B,C\cup H,s,a,b,(c,h))\leftrightarrow(A,B\cup H,C,s,a,(b,h),c)\) when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp H\mid B,C,S_s\) in \(G_{\overline B,\underline H}\). Rule \(3\) maps \((A,B\cup H,C,s,a,(b,h),c)\leftrightarrow(A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\) when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp H\mid B,C,S_s\) in \(G_{\overline B,\overline{H_s(C)}}\). Each displayed reverse and each cell \((a,b,c,h)\) is a separate canonical move instance. The \(\mathrm{popfix}_r\) tags have \(s=\mathrm{pop}\), and \(\mathrm{selfix}_r\) have \(s=\mathrm{sel}\), so the latter condition every separation test on \(S=1\). Disjointness of \(A,B,C,H\), nonemptiness of \(A,H\), membership of both scalar keys in \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and definition of the displayed input cell are mandatory.

semantic_closure.name: Exact margin-extension and population-storage transitions
semantic_closure.construction: Margin extension has arity two at each cell. For nonempty \(Z\subseteq V\setminus T_0\), fixed \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\), and fixed \(z\in\mathcal X_Z\), its only input keys are \((Z,\varnothing,T_0,\mathrm{sel},z,\ast,t)\) and \((T_0,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},t,\ast,\ast)\). If \(Z\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid T_0\) in \(\mathcal G\) and the selected conditional cell is defined, the output is \((T_0\cup Z,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},(t,z),\ast,\ast)\), with annotation equal to the product of the two input annotations. Population storage has arity one at each \((a,b,c)\): input \((A,B,C,\mathrm{sel},a,b,c)\), output \((A,B,C,\mathrm{pop},a,b,c)\), and unchanged annotation when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C\) in \(G_{\overline B}\). Every conditioning cell used by an input must have positive probability. These are the only source-changing moves, and every output belongs to \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\).

semantic_closure.name: Canonical finite mixed-source saturation machine
semantic_closure.construction: On input \((\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0,q_S,q_0)\), \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) initializes, for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\), the scalar key \((V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{sel},v,\ast,\ast)\) with annotation \(q_S(v)\) and provenance \(\mathrm{init}_S\). When \(T_0\ne\varnothing\), it also initializes, for every \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\), \((T_0,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},t,\ast,\ast)\) with \(q_0(t)\) and provenance \(\mathrm{init}_0\); when \(T_0=V\), these are exactly all cells of the full population law. When \(T_0=\varnothing\), \(q_0\) is the unique trivial law, its scalar unit creates no key, and no margin-extension instance is admissible because its required nonempty population-margin input key is absent. Population storage remains admissible whenever its unchanged predicate \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C\) in \(G_{\overline B}\) holds, including the corresponding unconditional selection-independence predicate when \(B=C=\varnothing\). At each state the scalar target key \((Y,X,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},y,x,\ast)\) is checked first. Otherwise the procedure scans \(\mathscr U\) in the order \(\mathrm{popstore},\mathrm{margin},\mathrm{popfix}_1,\mathrm{popfix}_2,\mathrm{popfix}_3,\mathrm{selfix}_1,\mathrm{selfix}_2,\mathrm{selfix}_3,\mathrm{marginal},\mathrm{condition},\mathrm{chain}\), then lexicographically, and takes the first instance whose exact premises hold, whose complete finite input-key set is contained in \(K_\sigma\), and whose one output scalar key is absent. It adds that output key, stores the displayed scalar arithmetic annotation and backpointer, and preserves all old entries. A present output is a duplicate and is skipped without overwrite. The target annotation is returned as \(F_{x,y}\); if no enabled instance has an absent output, \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) is returned. Formula spelling and derivation length never affect key identity or priority.

semantic_closure.statement: Fix \(\epsilon>0\) and \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\). At every reachable state \(\sigma\), \(K_\sigma\subseteq\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and every present scalar key \(\xi=(A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\) has exactly one scalar annotation and backpointer in \(E_\sigma\). For every \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), that annotation equals the cell \(k_\kappa^M(a\mid b,c)=P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s)\) whenever the conditioning cell is positive. Every transition has exactly the finite input-key set, source tags, graphical predicate, denominator condition, scalar output key, and stored scalar functional specified by its move definition. No move overwrites a key or uses an annotation as a state identity, and only margin extension or population storage changes a selected source into a population source.
semantic_closure.justification: This invariant is the formal firewall preventing a conditional selected table from being silently reused as a population kernel.
semantic_closure.gap: IDSB establishes soundness of its recursion; the enlarged saturation requires a key-level invariant that audits every probability, graphical-fixing, and source-bridge transition without treating formulas as state identities.
semantic_closure.consumer: A checker can replay each ACTG audit formula from its backpointers and reject any derivation that crosses source tags without a licensed bridge.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
We prove the assertion by induction on the number of transitions from the initialized state in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\).

At initialization, the selected key indexed by a full cell \(v\) has annotation
\[
 q_S(v)=P_M(V=v\mid S=1),
\]
where the equality follows from membership of \(M\) in the exact fiber.  If \(T_0\neq\varnothing\), the population key indexed by \(t\) has annotation
\[
 q_0(t)=P_M(T_0=t).
\]
These are precisely the kernels named by their selected and population source tags.  The initialized keys belong to \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and each is assigned once with its prescribed initialization backpointer.

Assume the invariant before one transition.  For a marginalization transition, the induction hypothesis and finite additivity give, cell by cell,
\[
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal X_H}
 P_M(A=a,H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s)
 =P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s).
\]
For a conditioning transition, its required strict denominator condition and the induction hypothesis give
\[
 \frac{P_M(A=a,H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s)}
 {\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}P_M(A=a',H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s)}
 =P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,H=h,S_s).
\]
For a chain transition, the conditional product rule gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s)\\
 &\qquad{}\times
 P_M(H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,A=a,S_s)\\
 &=P_M(A=a,H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s).
 \end{aligned}
\]
All denominators invoked here are positive by the eligibility condition in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\).

For any population or selected graphical-fixing transition, the relevant equality is exactly one of the sound do-calculus equivalences in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}rules}\).  Its source tag is retained, and its conditioning cell is required to be positive.  For margin extension, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}margin\text{-}extension}\) gives at every eligible \((t,z)\)
\[
 P_M(T_0=t,Z=z)
 =P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t,S=1)q_0(t),
\]
which is the stored product.  Finally, for population storage the graphical premise \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C\) in \(G_{\overline B}\), the positive selected conditioning cell, and Rule 1 of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}rules}\) imply
\[
 P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S=1)
 =P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c).
\]
Thus every possible transition stores the model kernel named by its output key.

The transition definitions require their complete finite input-key sets to be present and their output to lie in \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) further requires that output to be absent, adds it once with one annotation and one backpointer, and preserves every old entry.  Therefore uniqueness and the inclusion \(K_\sigma\subseteq\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\) are preserved.  The list of move tags shows directly that probability and graphical-fixing moves retain \(s\), while the two source-bridge moves are the only transitions with selected input and population output.  This completes the induction.

semantic_closure.justification: The representation index and explicit step-size bound turn the null-space argument into a valid interior SCM construction rather than a model-level shorthand.
semantic_closure.gap: Kivva et al. perturb response laws under unnormalized source constraints; the normalized selected-law cross-product rows and independent margin rows are specific to this two-law fiber.
semantic_closure.consumer: A terminal graph construction only needs to establish query-row separation; this theorem then produces the exact paired witness with controlled atom masses.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Set
\[
 A_0=u^{\mathsf T}a_+,
 \qquad N_v=u^{\mathsf T}a_v,
 \qquad \delta_+=\beta^{\mathsf T}a_+,
 \qquad \delta_v=\beta^{\mathsf T}a_v.
\]
The law of total probability over the active atoms \(j\in\mathcal J_0\), with every other independent exogenous coordinate integrated out as in the row definitions, gives
\[
 P_M(V=v,S=1)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0}u_ja_v(j)=N_v,
 \qquad
 P_M(S=1)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0}u_ja_+(j)=A_0>0.
\]
The last inequality follows from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}represented\text{-}interior\text{-}class}\): membership there entails membership in the exact fiber, whose defining model-class membership includes \(P_M(S=1)>0\). Therefore
\[
 q_S(v)=\frac{N_v}{A_0}.
\]
The same total-probability calculation, using the definitions of \(b_t\) and \(h_{x,y}\), gives
\[
 q_0(t)=P_M(T_0=t)=u^{\mathsf T}b_t,
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(M)=u^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}.
\]

The space \(\mathbb R^{\mathcal J_0}\) is finite-dimensional because \(\mathcal J_0\) is finite. Since \(h_{x,y}\notin\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}\), its orthogonal residual
\[
 \beta=h_{x,y}-\operatorname{proj}_{\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}}h_{x,y}
\]
belongs to \(\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}^\perp\), is nonzero, and satisfies
\[
 \beta^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}=\lVert\beta\rVert_2^2>0.
\]
Thus a direction with the property required in the statement exists. For any such chosen direction, orthogonality to the generators in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}projective\text{-}row\text{-}space}\) yields
\[
 \beta^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1=0,
 \qquad
 \beta^{\mathsf T}b_t=0,
 \qquad
 A_0\delta_v-N_v\delta_+=0
 \quad\text{for every }t,v.
\]

The step-size bound is defined because \(\beta\ne0\), hence \(\lVert\beta\rVert_\infty>0\). For every active atom, the response-interior hypothesis and the displayed bound on \(\tau\) give
\[
 u_j^{\pm}
 \geq u_j-\lvert\tau\rvert\lVert\beta\rVert_\infty
 \geq\frac{\eta}{2}>0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0}u_j^{\pm}
 =1\pm\tau\beta^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1=1.
\]
Thus both \(u^+\) and \(u^-\) are probability vectors on exactly the unchanged support \(\mathcal J_0\). Every other exogenous coordinate is unchanged and has every active atom mass at least \(\eta\); hence every coordinate atom of either perturbed representation has mass at least \(\eta/2\).

The row \(a_+\) is coordinatewise nonnegative. Since \(A_0=u^{\mathsf T}a_+>0\), at least one coordinate of \(a_+\) is positive. Every coordinate of \(u^\pm\) is positive, so
\[
 (u^\pm)^{\mathsf T}a_+=A_0\pm\tau\delta_+>0.
\]
For each \(v\), the cross-product equality above gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac{(u^\pm)^{\mathsf T}a_v}{(u^\pm)^{\mathsf T}a_+}
 &=\frac{N_v\pm\tau\delta_v}{A_0\pm\tau\delta_+}\\
 &=\frac{N_v}{A_0}=q_S(v).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, the second equality follows by cross multiplication from \(A_0\delta_v=N_v\delta_+\), and both denominators are positive. Similarly,
\[
 (u^\pm)^{\mathsf T}b_t
 =u^{\mathsf T}b_t\pm\tau\beta^{\mathsf T}b_t
 =q_0(t).
\]
Hence the two perturbations reproduce both observed tables exactly and preserve every selected lower bound \(q_S(v)\geq\epsilon\).

Only the mass vector of the independent coordinate \(U_0\) changes. All deterministic response maps, their parent arguments, and all other independent exogenous laws remain fixed. Thus the induced models remain recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with \(\mathcal G\). The preceding equalities and positivity place the perturbed triples in
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\epsilon,\eta/2}^{\circ}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0).
\]
In particular, both models lie in \(\mathfrak F_\epsilon(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), and their observation maps are exactly \((q_S,q_0)\). Finally,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)-\psi_{x,y}(M_2)
 &=(u+\tau\beta)^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}-(u-\tau\beta)^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}\\
 &=2\tau\beta^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}\ne0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Each scalar query is a convex combination of entries of \(h_{x,y}\in[0,1]^{\mathcal J_0}\), so it lies in \([0,1]\). This proves every assertion.
